observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] FlashPlaceholderWrapper accepts any digits through `flash(?::(\\d+):(\\d+))?:(.+)` and builds `new FlashEffect(innerPlaceholder, on, off)` with no range check (FlashPlaceholderWrapper.java:67-70). applyWithFade then computes `long cycleDuration = flashDuration + hideDuration;` and `long position = currentTick % cycleDuration;`, so `flash:0:0:%x%` throws ArithmeticException out of placeholder resolution, and a value too large for a long throws NumberFormatException from `Long.parseLong(flashOn)`. Both come from user-authored placeholder strings. The layer is unwired today (#5), hence P3.

title: CooldownPlaceholderProvider's raw token truncates to 0 while the cooldown is still active
fix: Round the raw seconds up (ceil of millis/1000) so an active cooldown never renders 0, matching CooldownFormat.human's minimum of 1s
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] The raw form renders `Long.toString(remaining.toSeconds())`, and Duration.toSeconds truncates, so for the last 999 ms of any cooldown `%cooldown_<id>%` shows 0 while CooldownService.isActive still returns true. A message such as "wait %cooldown_x% seconds" therefore tells the player to wait 0 seconds while the action is still refused. The formatted sibling of the same token disagrees in that window, because CooldownFormat.human clamps to `Math.max(duration.toSeconds(), 1)` and shows 1s.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: Held items are lost on Escape and on disconnect - MenuListener's tracked close branch untracks and calls onClose but never returns an ItemHoldingComponent's contents
fix: default void returnHeldItemsOnUserClose(Player) on MenuTarget, called after untrack in the tracked close branch; ChestMenu overrides it with the guarded return
observation: The bug Oriel independently fixed as its own menu-chest #1 (ChestMenuCloseListener.java:69-73 there). CraftBukkit closes the inventory before PlayerQuitEvent fires (SPIGOT-5799), so onQuit finds nothing tracked and the PLAYER_DISCONNECT return path is dead code; MenuListener was final and MenuTarget had no user-close hook, so nothing could restore the item. FIXED fix round 1 (2026-09-17): MenuTarget.java:103 default hook, MenuListener.java:165-169/182-190, ChestMenu.java:247-250.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: ItemComponent/adoptComponentsFrom leak and reset the builder-marked interactive flag, and fill decoration overwrites it, producing a stale-flag leak plus an infinite free-item fill exploit on rerender
fix: Decoration must never override a builder-interactive slot: clear the interactive flag wherever handlers are cleared, have adoptComponentsFrom adopt the fresh interactiveSlots set, and have fill/renderAll skip interactive slots
tests: ChestMenuTest (post-render assertions, fix rounds 1-2), ChestMenuBuilderTest (fix round 1)
observation: Three-part bug found in the E6.1 review: (a) ItemComponent's render call to view.interactive(false) made builder.interactive(slot).fill(X) non-interactive after the first render; (b) dropped/empty components cleared handlers but not the interactive flag; (c) adoptComponentsFrom did not adopt fresh.interactiveSlots. FIXED fix round 1 (a/b/c), but the fix round 1 re-review found two NEW regressions from the fix itself: N1 rerenderSlot/the untouched-render branch cleared a builder-marked interactive flag instead of preserving it, and N2 fill decoration started landing in interactive slots (infinite free fill items via take+rerender). FIXED fix round 2 (2026-09-20): interactive slots floored/restored (ChestMenu.java:85,406,517; ChestMenuBuilder.java:254) and fill skips them (:526,573).

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: COLLECT_TO_CURSOR on an interactive top-inventory slot collects the item, bypassing the interactive-slot click policy that blocks every other action
fix: Cancel the click before the interactive check succeeds, unless handleDepositClick explicitly accepted it
observation: The click-policy matrix blocked every other action on a non-deposit interactive slot but let COLLECT_TO_CURSOR through, letting a player vacuum items out of slots the menu never intended to be collectible from. The same shape exists today in Gangland's own custom inventory framework (InventoryClickHandler.java:34-43, gangland-ui/inventory-api) - Gangland's own docket row (T-41) notes this is fixed by its WS2 cutover onto keystone-inventory. FIXED fix round 1 (2026-09-17).

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: A menu veto followed by the player disconnecting before the scheduled reopen fires loses the held item permanently; a plugin reload/disable landing inside that same veto-to-reopen window loses it too
fix: Record a pending reopen per InventoryService when a tracked close is vetoed; consume it atomically on PlayerQuitEvent and return the held items with PLAYER_DISCONNECT (quit fires before player data saves); drain any still-pending reopen from closeAll(RELOAD/PLUGIN_DISABLE) and onPreClear/onShutdown too, not only from onQuit
tests: InventoryServiceLifecycleTest:69-98 (drain/reload case, fix round 3), MenuListenerTest:539 (exactly-once veto+quit case, fix round 2)
observation: Found by the E6.1 fix round 1 re-review as a pre-existing gap (also present in Oriel's own listener pair - see that project's docket twin row) while confirming the F1 fix. FIXED across fix rounds 2 and 3 (2026-09-17 to 2026-09-20): round 2 added the per-service pendingReopen record/consume on veto+quit; the round 2 re-review found closeAll(RELOAD/PLUGIN_DISABLE) still did not drain it (a reload inside the veto-to-reopen window still lost the item, since the vetoed player was already untracked before the record); round 3 closed that gap with an atomic Set.copyOf snapshot drain in closeAll plus onPreClear/onShutdown hooks, and a same-instance tracked+pending conflict is structurally impossible since untrack always precedes record.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: ChestMenu.close(Player) calls tracker().untrack(player) unconditionally; if menu B was opened while menu A was still live, A's later programmatic close untracks the player from B, so B's Escape then misses MenuListener's tracked branch and B's held items are silently discarded
fix: Untrack only when service.tracker().currentMenuOf(player) == this, not unconditionally
observation: A close(Player) call from menu A (e.g. a stale reference kept past a switch, or two independent InventoryService consumers racing) blindly calls the shared tracker's untrack(player) regardless of which menu the tracker currently associates with that player. If the player has since moved on to menu B, A's close silently steals B's tracking entry, so when the player then presses Escape on B, MenuListener's tracked-close branch (the one that returns held items, see row 1/4 above) never fires for B - its ItemHoldingComponent contents are discarded with no error. Not reachable from Gangland's npc-shops today (its flows do not hold two live menus for one player simultaneously), but a real hazard for any future multi-menu consumer. Found by the WS2 G4 lead, seconded by the review.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: A disconnect during a suspend() detour is swallowed by suppressClose(), so end() never runs and the flow's FlowCloseListener is never unregistered - one leaked listener holding a dead Player per abandoned anvil-style prompt
fix: Add a PlayerQuitEvent handler on the flow (or clear the suspended flag on quit) so a disconnect mid-detour still runs the normal end()/unregister path
observation: When a flow is suspended for an external detour (anvil prompt, sign edit, etc.) and the player disconnects instead of completing the detour, suppressClose() treats the resulting close event as expected and swallows it, so end() is never called and the FlowCloseListener Bukkit registered for that flow is never unregistered - it leaks for the plugin's uptime, holding a reference to the now-offline Player. Reachable today through Gangland's BankerAmountView, BankerCreateAccountView, BankerRenameAccountView and QuantitySelectorView (all suspend() during an anvil prompt). Found by the WS2 G4 lead, seconded by the review.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: MenuFlow.rerender() and switchTo() have no `if (ended) return;` guard (openAt() has one), so a task scheduled before end() can still write into an already-closed inventory
fix: Add the same `if (ended) return;` guard rerender()/switchTo() that openAt() already has
observation: openAt() already guards against running after end() with `if (ended) return;`, but rerender() and switchTo() do not, so a task scheduled while the flow was still live (e.g. a delayed recompute) can fire after end() and write into an inventory that has already been closed and torn down. Harmless today - Gangland's BarterView.scheduleRecompute is the only known caller in this shape, and its own cleanup already tends to beat the scheduled task in practice - but the guard is structurally missing. Found by the WS2 G4 lead, seconded by the review.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: Keystone compiles keystone-inventory against Bukkit 1.16.5, where InventoryView is a class; a consumer on 1.21.x (Gangland pins 1.21.11) sees it as an interface, so keystone-inventory bytecode calling ChestMenu.close(Player, CloseReason) throws IncompatibleClassChangeError against any mocked Player in a consumer's unit test
fix: A Keystone test-support helper that hides the version gap, or compile keystone-inventory's own module against a 1.21 api while keeping plugin.yml's api-version at 1.16
location: keystone-inventory module (compiled against Bukkit 1.16.5); consumer-side symptom in Gangland's item-survival tests
observation: Live servers are unaffected: Keystone's plugin.yml declares api-version 1.16 and CraftBukkit's Commodore rewrites the InventoryView class/interface mismatch transparently at the packet/reflection layer server-side. The gap only bites a consumer's own unit tests, which run against the raw 1.21.x Bukkit API/mocks with no Commodore rewrite in play - Gangland's item-survival tests currently wrap the call in a documented catch (closeIgnoringKnownBukkitVersionGap) to route around it rather than fail. Test-fragility tier (P2), not a live-server bug. Found by the WS2 G4 lead, seconded by the review.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: Opening another menu of the same InventoryService over a menu with held items (ctx.openMenu, openPrevious, registry.open, B.open) skips returnHeldItemsOnUserClose and discards A's held items
fix: In MenuListener.onClose also call target.returnHeldItemsOnUserClose(player) on the non-tracked branch (safe: close(Player, reason) already cleared the held state, and the guarded return no-ops on an empty held list)
tests: ChestMenuTest:237 covers only the reverse (stale close of A with B holding); nothing covers A holding then B opened
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] ChestMenu.open tracks the incoming menu before opening it (`service.tracker().track(player, this);` then `player.openInventory(inventory);`, ChestMenu.java:215-217), so the InventoryCloseEvent CraftBukkit fires for the outgoing menu A sees `service.tracker().currentMenuOf(player) == target` false and skips the whole tracked branch, including `target.returnHeldItemsOnUserClose(player);` (MenuListener.java:184); only `target.onClose(event, player)` runs. Trigger: any menu with an ItemHoldingComponent (Oriel deposit slot, a trade-input tray) plus a navigation button using ClickContext.openMenu/openPrevious (ChestClickContext.java:86,91 route to InMemoryMenuRegistry.doOpen -> menu.open) or a direct B.open(player). A's Bukkit inventory is discarded with the item in it: permanent item loss. MenuTarget.returnHeldItemsOnUserClose's own doc (MenuTarget.java:93-95) promises the return for opening another inventory, which only holds when the other inventory is not a menu of the same service.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: ClickContext.closeMenu() goes through the plain ChestMenu.close(Player), which untracks before closeInventory, so a Close button discards every ItemHoldingComponent's items
fix: Have ChestClickContext.closeMenu() call menu.close(player, CloseReason.USER) (the returning overload), or fold into the KS-IV-09 fix so the non-tracked close branch also returns held items
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] `public void closeMenu() { menu.close(player); }` reaches ChestMenu.close(Player) (ChestMenu.java:240-247), which runs `service.tracker().untrack(player);` and then `player.closeInventory();`; the resulting close event fails MenuListener's `currentMenuOf(player) == target` check, so returnHeldItemsOnUserClose never runs and the plain overload returns nothing by itself. ClickContext.closeMenu is the only close exposed to click handlers and its doc is just 'Close the current menu for the player', so a deposit or input menu with a standard Close button loses whatever the player put in. docs/keystone-inventory.md:72-75 documents that the plain overload does not return items, but not that the canonical click-context close uses it.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: ChestMenu.adoptComponentsFrom drains an ItemHoldingComponent only when its slot vanishes; a slot that a different component replaces loses the held items on an in-place MenuFlow switch
fix: Drain when fresh.components.get(oldSlot) != outgoing (identity), not only when the slot is absent from fresh
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] The drain is gated on `if (!fresh.components.containsKey(oldSlot)) { ... if (outgoing instanceof ItemHoldingComponent held) { returnHeldItemsForSlot(...` and then `components.clear(); components.putAll(fresh.components);` drops the outgoing component unconditionally. Trigger: MenuFlow.switchTo to a different panel with the same size and title (the in-place branch, MenuFlow.java:295-302) where panel A has a deposit or holding component at slot 13 and panel B puts any other component (a confirm button) at slot 13. The holding component is removed from the map without a return, renderAll overwrites the physical slot with B's item, and no later close path (returnHeldItems iterates `components`) can find it again: item loss. The same happens on MenuFlow.rerender() if Panel.render builds a new holding-component instance per render. docs/keystone-inventory.md:67 only promises the drain for a dropped slot.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: renderAll never clears a re-rendered slot's old handlers, so click kinds bound by the previous component (outgoing panel, previous page) stay live and fire
fix: clearHandlers(slot) before renderOne for every component slot in renderAll/rerenderSlot (renderInto rebinds what it needs), not only on the untouched branch
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] renderAll clears handlers only for components that rendered nothing (`if (!touched) { inventory.setItem(entry.getKey(), null); clearHandlers(entry.getKey());`); a touched slot keeps every previously bound ClickKind because SlotHandlers.set replaces only the kinds the new component sets (SlotHandlers.java:24-26) and ItemComponent.renderInto binds only its non-null handlers (ItemComponent.java:127-135). adoptComponentsFrom clears handlers only for slots missing from fresh (ChestMenu.java:396). Trigger: an in-place MenuFlow switch or rerender where slot N had onAnyClick(buy) and now holds a component with only onLeftClick(confirm); a right, middle, drop or number-key click resolves to the stale ANY handler and runs the old panel's action. PagedRegion makes it routine: an entry with a handler on page 1 (`component.onAnyClick(entry.handler())`, PagedRegion.java:66-67) followed by a handler-less Entry(item) at the same cell on page 2 keeps firing page 1's handler after an in-place page change.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: ChestMenu.open() on a menu the player is already viewing runs MenuListener's tracked close branch on itself: untracks the player, fires on_close, and returns held items still rendered in the slot
fix: In ChestMenu.open, untrack (or skip the re-track) before openInventory when currentMenuOf(player) == this, or have MenuListener.onClose ignore a close whose menu is being reopened (a reopening flag set around openInventory)
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] open() does `service.tracker().track(player, this); renderAll(player); player.openInventory(inventory);`; when the player's top inventory is already this menu (same or, after ensureTitleFor rebuilt it, the previous inventory), CraftBukkit fires InventoryCloseEvent for it first, and MenuListener sees `service.tracker().currentMenuOf(player) == target` true (MenuListener.java:155), so it untracks the player, calls returnHeldItemsOnUserClose, and dispatches the on_close handler. The player ends up viewing the menu while untracked: a later Escape takes the non-tracked branch (held items deposited afterwards are lost), vetoClose no longer applies, and closeAll(RELOAD/PLUGIN_DISABLE) does not close it. The held items were returned while the component's rendering still shows them in the slot (renderAll ran before openInventory), so an interactive holding slot can be emptied a second time: duplication. Trigger: re-opening a live menu, which is the only way to apply a changed %placeholder% title (ensureTitleFor runs only from open, ChestMenu.java:485-499), or a MenuRegistry factory that returns a cached menu instance.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: MenuFlow's FlowCloseListener ends the flow on a close that MenuListener vetoed; the next-tick reopen then shows a menu whose flow is dead
fix: Have FlowCloseListener skip end() when the closing menu vetoes the close (holder.target().vetoesClose(player)), or have MenuListener expose the pending reopen so the flow can check service.consumePendingReopen state
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] FlowCloseListener.onClose calls `end()` whenever `holder.target() == currentMenu && event.getPlayer().equals(viewer)` and suppressClose() is false; it never consults vetoesClose. When a panel sets ChestMenuBuilder.vetoClose, MenuListener (registered first at bootstrap) untracks, records a pending reopen and schedules `menu.open(player)` (MenuListener.java:156-178), while the flow listener runs end(): onEnd fires, held items are returned, and the close listener is unregistered. Next tick the dead flow's menu reopens and is tracked; its buttons call switchTo/back, which no-op on `if (ended) return;` (MenuFlow.java:166,193), and each Escape re-triggers the veto. The player sits in a window whose navigation does nothing and cannot close it while the predicate holds.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: MenuFlow.end() from FlowCloseListener calls ChestMenu.close, which calls player.closeInventory() inside the InventoryCloseEvent; the nested close dispatches the menu's on_close handler twice
fix: In ChestMenu.close(Player) skip closeInventory when invoked from the close of this same inventory (or have FlowCloseListener end the flow without closing: return held items and untrack only)
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] On Escape, MenuListener.onClose dispatches `target.onClose(event, player)` once, then FlowCloseListener calls end() -> `currentMenu.close(viewer, CloseReason.NAVIGATION)` (MenuFlow.java:270) -> close(Player), where `if (player.getOpenInventory().getTopInventory() == inventory) { player.closeInventory(); }` is still true because the view is only swapped after the event. CraftBukkit's closeInventory re-fires InventoryCloseEvent with no reentrancy guard, so MenuListener runs again (now on the non-tracked branch) and dispatches on_close a second time. Any non-idempotent on_close handler on a flow panel (message, refund, releaseHold-style cleanup) runs twice per Escape.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: An in-place MenuFlow switch keeps the outgoing panel's vetoClose, onClose/onOpen, clickDelay, permission, name, placeholders and fill; adoptComponentsFrom copies only components
fix: Adopt the per-panel settings too (closeVeto, onCloseHandler, onOpenHandler, clickDelayMillis, requiredPermission, name, placeholders; make fillComponent non-final and adopt it), or restrict the in-place branch to panels with identical settings
tests: MenuFlowTest.switchToADifferentPanelWithMatchingSizeAndTitleSwitchesInPlace asserts only menu identity and panel id
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] adoptComponentsFrom copies `components`, `interactiveSlots` and `builderInteractiveSlots` from the throwaway menu and nothing else; `fillComponent` is final (ChestMenu.java:68). switchInternal's in-place branch (MenuFlow.java:295-302) uses it for any different panel with the same rows and title, so panel B's `.vetoClose(...)`, `.onClose(...)`, `.clickDelay(...)` and `.fill(...)` are silently ignored and panel A's stay in force (A's veto can trap the player on B; B's on_close cleanup never runs). The full-reopen branch builds a real menu with B's settings, so behaviour differs depending only on whether two panels happen to share a title.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: KS-IV-02 fix is incomplete: border and line decoration still render into builder-interactive slots, so a take-and-rerender still mints free decoration items
fix: Skip border and line placement for slots in interactiveSlots in ChestMenuBuilder.build (as renderAll already does for fill)
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] KS-IV-02 set the invariant that decoration never overrides a builder-interactive slot but applied it only to fill (ChestMenu.java:535,582). build() still does `if (border != null) applyBorder(finalSlots, size); for (LineComponent line : lines) applyLine(finalSlots, line, size);` without consulting `interactiveSlots`, so the border or line component sits in `components` for that slot and renderAll re-renders it on every pass while the slot stays interactive (floor). Trigger: `.rows(1).border(M).interactive(4)` (with rows 1 or 2 every slot is border, applyBorder at ChestMenuBuilder.java:279-289) or a line through an input slot; the player takes the pane, the next rerender puts it back.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: A vetoed-close reopen that open() refuses (permission gate, subclass view gate) consumes the pending entry and never returns the held items
fix: In the scheduled reopen, return stillPending's held items when the menu is not tracked after menu.open(player) (open refused)
tests: MenuListenerTest:539 covers veto then quit only
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] The veto branch untracks without returning held items, and the next-tick task does `MenuTarget stillPending = service.consumePendingReopen(playerId); ... if (player.isOnline()) { menu.open(player); }`. ChestMenu.open returns early when `!player.hasPermission(requiredPermission)` (ChestMenu.java:207-210), and a subclass open gate (Oriel's view requirements) can refuse the same way. The pending entry is already consumed, the player is untracked and not viewing the menu, and no later path (onQuit, closeAll) can find the held items: item loss. Trigger: permission revoked, or a view requirement turning false, between the vetoed close and the next tick.

sysName: Keystone · Menu / inventory framework (Phase E6, added 2026-09-17)
title: InMemoryMenuRegistry.open records a NavigationHistory entry even when the menu's open() was refused by its permission gate, so openPrevious lands on the wrong menu
fix: Record only when the player is actually tracked on the new menu after open (service tracker check), or have Menu.open report refusal
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] `boolean opened = doOpen(player, name); if (opened) { history.recordOpen(player.getUniqueId(), name); }`, and doOpen returns true whenever `menu.open(player)` does not throw (InMemoryMenuRegistry.java:88-94); ChestMenu.open returns normally after `noPermissionHandler.accept(player); return;` (ChestMenu.java:207-210). Trigger: a button doing ctx.openMenu("admin") for a player lacking the permission while in menu main: the trail becomes [.., main, admin] although the player never left main, and a Back button then pops admin and reopens main instead of the menu before it.

sysName: Keystone · Shop framework, headless (Phase H10, added 2026-09-20; promoted from Gangland's gangland-ui/shop-api)
title: DefaultShopDisplayResolverTest lost the live-name-before-pristine pin (informally "T-R4") when GanglandShopDisplayResolverTest was deleted at the Gangland-side shop-api promotion
fix: One more test in DefaultShopDisplayResolverTest registering a serializer/converter pair whose pristine rebuild returns a different display name than the live one, asserting live wins - ported from the deleted GanglandShopDisplayResolverTest
tests: FIXED - new test in DefaultShopDisplayResolverTest (commit b706f30, branch phase-e6-inventory): red under inverted precedence (asserts pristine wins), green after revert to the real live-first precedence; production DefaultShopDisplayResolver code untouched
observation: When Gangland's gangland-ui/shop-api module was deleted and its 26 headless classes promoted into keystone-shop (Keystone's own earlier G0), DefaultShopDisplayResolver (the promoted GanglandShopDisplayResolver) carried over cleanly, but its existing DefaultShopDisplayResolverTest only ever supplied a live name with no competing non-null pristine value (ItemDefinitions.pristine returns null for an unregistered stack), so it could not distinguish live-first precedence from pristine-first. The deleted GanglandShopDisplayResolverTest had registered a serializer/converter pair whose pristine rebuild returned a different display name and asserted live wins - that specific two-source-conflict pin was lost at promotion and nothing in keystone-shop's own suite caught it (a coverage gap, not a live production regression - the resolver's actual precedence logic was never touched). Found in the Gangland WS4 G1a review (Important 1, informally referenced there and in the WS2/WS4 dispatch as "T-R4"); fixed by a test-only commit on wt/keystone-1.11.0 (b706f30), dispatched upstream in parallel with the Gangland-side fix round per orchestrator ruling W45.

sysName: Keystone · Shop framework, headless (Phase H10, added 2026-09-20; promoted from Gangland's gangland-ui/shop-api)
title: ShopPurchaseService.purchase accepts a negative finalTotal; a negative YAML Price credits the buyer via withdraw
fix: Return a failure outcome when finalTotal is null or signum() < 0 (mirror ShopSellService's signum guard) and have ShopYamlReader.parsePrice reject negative Price/Base_Price with a warning instead of accepting them
tests: ShopPurchaseServiceTest, ShopYamlReaderTest (neither covers a negative amount)
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] purchase clamps `if (copies < 1) copies = 1;` but never validates the money side: `if (payment.getBalance().compareTo(finalTotal) < 0)` passes for any negative total and `payment.withdraw(finalTotal);` is called with it, then the item is delivered anyway. ShopYamlReader.parsePrice (ShopYamlReader.java:44-53) accepts any sign, so an admin typo `Price: -50` in a shop YAML loads as a live buy entry. The documented adapter path (Gangland TraderBuyListener.adapt -> EconomyHandler.withdrawAmount, keystone-hooks EconomyHandler.java:72-77) only rejects `normalised.compareTo(current) > 0` and then `setAmount(current.subtract(normalised))`, so a negative withdraw adds money: every click hands the player the item plus 50. ShopSellService already refuses `offeredTotal.signum() <= 0`; the purchase side has no equivalent guard.

sysName: Keystone · Shop framework, headless (Phase H10, added 2026-09-20; promoted from Gangland's gangland-ui/shop-api)
title: CategorySellValuator/CategoryBarterValuator round per-item price to 2dp before applying the ratio (double rounding)
fix: Keep perItem unrounded (divide with a wide scale, e.g. MathContext.DECIMAL64) and round once after multiplying by ratio*mood, in both valuators
tests: CategorySellValuatorTest, CategoryBarterValuatorTest (the HALF_UP pin at ratio 1.0 cannot tell single from double rounding)
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] value() computes `perItem = bundlePrice.divide(BigDecimal.valueOf(templateAmount), PRICE_SCALE, PRICE_MODE);` (already rounded to 0.01) and then `perItem.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(sellPriceRatio * moodMultiplier)).setScale(PRICE_SCALE, PRICE_MODE)` rounds a second time. For a cheap bundle this inflates payouts: Base_Price 0.50 for a 64-item template at sellPriceRatio 0.5 gives 0.0078125 -> 0.01, then 0.01 * 0.5 = 0.005 -> 0.01 per item, so selling the 64 stack pays 0.64 against an intended 0.25 and more than the bundle's own 0.50 base price - a buy-then-sell loop mints money when the same stack is also a buy entry at or below 0.64. Single rounding gives 0.0039 -> 0.00. CategoryBarterValuator.java:38-42 has the identical two-step rounding for barter offers.

sysName: Keystone · Shop framework, headless (Phase H10, added 2026-09-20; promoted from Gangland's gangland-ui/shop-api)
title: PurchaseOutcome.INVENTORY_FULL is never returned by ShopPurchaseService
fix: Delete INVENTORY_FULL (or document it as reserved) - overflow is always dropped at the player's feet and reported as SUCCESS
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] The enum advertises `INVENTORY_FULL` to integrations, but ShopPurchaseService.purchase (ShopPurchaseService.java:53-57) always drops leftovers with `dropItemNaturally` and returns `PurchaseResult.success(...)`; no code path constructs INVENTORY_FULL. Consumers carry dead switch arms for it (Gangland TraderBuyListener: "Service drops leftovers naturally; kept for exhaustiveness."), a dead feature that looks shipped.

title: Hologram stands are setPersistent(false) and never respawned after chunk unload - hologram vanishes while spawned stays true
fix: Detect stale stands with !armorStand.isValid() (not isDead) and respawn in update/updateLine/teleport, or listen for ChunkLoadEvent in HologramService and respawn holograms whose base chunk reloaded
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] createArmorStand marks every line `armorStand.setPersistent(false);` (Hologram.java:162-163, comment "Won't save to disk"), so when the hologram's chunk unloads (every player walks away from a non-spawn-chunk hologram) the server discards the stands and does not recreate them on chunk reload. Nothing in Hologram or HologramService notices: `spawned` stays true, update() only respawns when `lines.size() != text.length`, and every per-line path guards with `isArmorStandDead` = `armorStand == null || armorStand.isDead()` (L145-147), which on 1.16.5 is still false for an unloaded-and-unregistered entity (only isValid() flips) and on 1.17+ is true, so either setCustomName hits a dead reference or the line is skipped. Result: any hologram outside always-loaded chunks disappears permanently after the first unload, createUpdatingHologram's timer keeps running against the stale stands forever (its `!hologram.isSpawned()` self-cancel never fires), and the same happens after /kill @e[type=armor_stand]. Only removeHologram + createHologram brings it back.

title: hologramsByLocation keyed on the caller's uncloned Location, never re-keyed by teleport and removed by value-blind key
fix: Key on a clone (location.clone()), use hologramsByLocation.remove(key, hologram), and re-key through a HologramService.teleport(id, loc) instead of Hologram.teleport mutating baseLocation in place
observation: [found 2026-09-24, master 4192baa] createHologram stores `hologramsByLocation.put(location, hologram);` with the caller's own mutable Location object (the Hologram keeps a clone as baseLocation), and removeHologram deletes with `hologramsByLocation.remove(hologram.getBaseLocation());` (L98-105). Three reachable divergences: (a) Hologram.teleport (Hologram.java:117-139) rewrites baseLocation in place but the map key stays at the old position, so after a teleport removeHologram misses the entry, getHologramAt(old) keeps returning the removed, despawned hologram and removeHologramAt(old) is a permanent no-op on it (leak), while getHologramAt(new) finds nothing; (b) a caller that reuses its Location (the common `loc.add(0, 1, 0)` between creates) changes the key's hashCode after insertion, stranding the entry the same way; (c) two holograms created at the same location - the second put overwrites the first, and removing the first then deletes the second's entry because remove is not value-checked, making the live second hologram unreachable by location.

title: Weapon.modifiersData is null for any weapon YAML without a Modifiers section and is dereferenced unguarded at 15 sites
fix: Initialise the field as `private ModifiersData modifiersData = new ModifiersData();` so every caller sees an empty, non-null ModifiersData
observation: `private ModifiersData modifiersData;` has no initialiser, and ModifiersSectionParser.apply() opens with `MappingNode modifiersSection = root.get("Modifiers").asMapping().orNull(); if (modifiersSection == null) return;` so a weapon YAML with no `Modifiers:` section leaves the field null. Fifteen call sites then dereference it with no guard, including `ProjectileState.canPenetrateBlock/canPenetrateEntity/canRicochet` (ProjectileState.java:66-93), `WeaponRaytracerImpl.java:501,515,555`, `ModifierHandler.java:96,121` and the flat-damage lookup in all five action classes. All 26 shipped weapon YAMLs carry a Modifiers section, so this is an authoring trap rather than a default-config break, but a server author writing an ordinary weapon with no modifiers gets an NPE on every shot that reaches these paths. Was Gangland WP-7.

title: SpreadManager.checkSpreadReset compares a tick-authored Time value against a millisecond delta
fix: Multiply spreadData.getResetTime() by 50 before the comparison, or track lastShotTime in ticks
observation: checkSpreadReset computes `long timeSinceLastShot = currentTime - lastShotTime;` from System.currentTimeMillis() and compares it with `if (timeSinceLastShot >= spreadData.getResetTime())`. The YAML authors that value in ticks — rifle.yml ships `Time: 5` under a comment reading "The time before the spread value is reset", meaning 5 ticks or 250ms. Read as 5 milliseconds, any real firing cadence exceeds it, so currentSpread is reset to Starting_Spread on effectively every shot and spread never accumulates toward its configured bounds. Was Gangland WP-8.

title: ReloadType.amount is a mutable field on a JVM-wide enum constant, shared by every weapon of that reload type
fix: Move Reload_Amount onto ReloadData per weapon and pass it into createInstance explicitly instead of reading enum state
observation: The enum declares `@Setter private int amount;` on constants INSTANT/ONE/NUM, which are singletons, and `createInstance` reads it via `case ONE, NUM -> new NumberedReload(weapon, ammunition, amount);`. Each weapon parser calls ReloadType.NUM.setAmount(...) at load time, so the last weapon parsed wins and every weapon of that reload type constructed afterwards reloads with that weapon's Reload_Amount. Two weapons configured with `num` reload and different Reload_Amount values silently reload by the same wrong number of rounds. Was Gangland WP-16.

title: WeaponService.weapons map is never pruned per player; only a full clear() on bean reload removes entries
fix: Remove a player's minted weapon uuids on PlayerQuitEvent and on item destruction, or hold them in a TTL/weak-keyed store
observation: `private final Map<UUID, Weapon> weapons;` only ever shrinks through `public void clear() { weapons.clear(); }`, whose sole caller is the WeaponManager.onClear() bean-reload hook — there is no removal tied to a player quitting, dying, or the item being destroyed. Every `/bartizan weapon give` registers a permanent entry, and WeaponManager.initialize() wires `repository.setDataSupplier(() -> getWeapons().values())`, so the map is also what gets persisted. The map therefore grows for the whole server uptime between reloads; the backing table is only bounded because WeaponDataCleanupTask calls repo.deleteAll() on a 30-day schedule. Was Gangland WP-9.

title: WeaponService.getWeapon(String) and getWeapon(Player,String) still mint and register a weapon on a read-only lookup
fix: Delete the two unused minting overloads, or make them delegate to createTransientWeapon so only an explicit give registers
tests: WeaponServiceTest.getWeaponTemplate_registersNothing and createTransientWeapon_registersNothing (prove the safe methods, not these two)
observation: getWeapon(String) forwards with uuid=null into the 4-arg overload, which unconditionally runs `Weapon finalWeapon = weaponAddon.copyWithUUID(finalUuid); weapons.put(finalUuid, finalWeapon);` — so any read-only lookup through these overloads grows the registry and the persisted weapon table by one row per call. Downgraded from the original P0: the api/plugin split narrowed the public WeaponCatalog to getWeaponTemplate, getWeaponTemplates, createTransientWeapon, validateAndGetWeapon and isWeapon, none of which mint, and the only in-repo caller of the minting path is WeaponGiveCommand with newInstance=true, where registration is intended. The two read overloads are now unused public methods that remain a trap for the next caller. Was Gangland WP-6, no longer reachable at P0 severity.

title: mintUuid gives every throwable of a type one deterministic UUID, so all players share one press-lock and one registry entry
fix: Key registered throwable instances and the WeaponInteract press maps by player plus type, keeping the deterministic uuid only for createTransientWeapon's inventory stacking
observation: mintUuid returns `UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes(("throwable:" + type)...)` for every THROWABLE-category weapon regardless of caller, documented as intentional so identical throwables stack in the inventory, and the give path then runs `weapons.put(finalUuid, finalWeapon)` with that shared uuid. Two consequences follow. Giving the same throwable type to a second player overwrites the first player's registered Weapon object at that key in the shared map. Worse, WeaponInteract.handleThrowablePress gates on isPressGated(weaponUuid) and engagePressHoldWatchdog(weaponUuid, ...) using that same shared uuid, so one player throwing a grenade press-locks every other online player holding that grenade type until the watchdog clears. Was Gangland WP-32.

title: Weapon.tags is a final Map copied by reference into every clone, and initClone clears the shared instance
fix: Drop final from the tags field and assign a fresh TreeMap in initClone instead of clearing the map the clone still shares
observation: `private final Map<WeaponTag, Object> tags;` is assigned once in the constructor as `this.tags = new TreeMap<>();` and, being final, can never be reassigned, so Object.clone() copies only the reference and every clone descended from the same config template shares one TreeMap. initClone() then calls `this.tags.clear();` at line 404, wiping the map its source and every sibling clone still point at. Item NBT stays correct because initializeTags()/updateTag() re-derive all four values from the weapon's own fields before writing, but the public getTags() getter returns another instance's or an already-cleared map's contents.

title: RecoilManager overrides clone() calling super.clone() without the class implementing Cloneable
fix: Implement Cloneable, or delete the dead clone() override since initClone() already builds a fresh RecoilManager
observation: The class is declared `public class RecoilManager {` with no `implements Cloneable`, yet overrides `public RecoilManager clone() { return (RecoilManager) super.clone(); }`. Object.clone() on a non-Cloneable type always throws CloneNotSupportedException, which this method wraps and rethrows, so the method can never succeed. It is currently unreachable because Weapon.initClone() constructs `new RecoilManager(this)` instead of calling it, making this dead code that will fail for the next caller who reasonably expects clone() to work. Was Gangland WP-34.

title: BiologicalAction.fireRay impact handler applies potion effects but never damages, so biological shots deal 0 HP
fix: In the impactHandler call target.damage(damage, player) for LivingEntity hits as IncendiaryAction does, or drop the custom handler so the raytracer's default damage path runs
observation: fire() computes `double damage = data.getBaseDamage() * level + flatBonus;` and passes it to fireRay, which sets `.baseDamage(damage)` but also supplies a custom `.impactHandler(event -> { if (event.getHitEntity() instanceof LivingEntity target) { for (PotionEffect effect : effects) target.addPotionEffect(effect); } })`. Verified in WeaponRaytracerImpl.java:426-437: a non-null impact handler runs and then `return;`s before the default `living.damage(event.getDamage(), shooter)` block at line 448, so the handler short-circuits damage entirely. Every charged biological shot applies only potion effects and zero health damage no matter what Base_Damage or charge level is configured. Was Gangland WP-3.

title: ThrowableAction EXPLOSIVE detonation damages twice and passes Explosion_Radius as vanilla explosion power
fix: Stop using createExplosion for damage (power 0 or a cosmetic-only burst) and let the manual WeaponRaytraceImpactEvent loop own the configured damage and radius
observation: detonate() calls `world.createExplosion(center.getX(), center.getY(), center.getZ(), (float) data.getExplosionRadius(), false, false, player);` — the trailing booleans suppress fire and block-breaking but NOT entity damage — then loops getNearbyEntities in the same radius and calls `target.damage(impactEvent.getDamage(), player)`. Anyone inside the blast takes vanilla explosion damage plus the full configured Explosion_Damage a second time. The fourth argument is explosion POWER, not radius: grenade.yml ships `Explosion_Radius: 4.0`, which is TNT-strength and reaches roughly 8 blocks, so entities 4-8 blocks out take vanilla damage the manual loop never intended to touch. Was Gangland WP-4.

title: MeleeAction and ThrowableAction never call weapon.consumeShot(), so configured magazines never deplete
fix: Call weapon.consumeShot() in MeleeAction.activate() and ThrowableAction.activate() gated on getAmmunitionData()/isMagazineEmpty() as the gun paths do
tests: WeaponConsumeShotTest (javadoc states it does not claim melee/throwable consume ammo in real play)
observation: MeleeAction.activate() guards with `if (weapon.getReloadData() != null && weapon.isMagazineEmpty())` but never calls consumeShot() anywhere in the class; ThrowableAction.activate() never references ammunitionData, reloadData or consumeShot at all and only decrements the held ItemStack. A repo-wide grep for `consumeShot()` returns only NpcWeaponControllerImpl, BiologicalAction, GunAction and IncendiaryAction. Any melee or throwable weapon authored with Ammunition:/Reload: sections has unlimited uses, because the isMagazineEmpty() guard reads a currentMagCapacity nothing ever decrements. Was Gangland WP-14 (melee/throwable half).

title: PluginFireRegistry.onShutdown() clears the tracked set without reverting the FIRE blocks it placed
fix: Iterate the tracked BlockVectors per world and reset each still-FIRE block to AIR before clearing the map
observation: The whole shutdown hook is `@Override public void onShutdown() { tracked.clear(); }`. Fire blocks placed by IncendiaryAction/ThrowableAction are reverted by per-block scheduled tasks, and those tasks are cancelled when the plugin disables, so any fire still burning at server stop or /reload is left in the world as a real block. Because tracked.clear() also erases the bookkeeping, PluginFireProtectionListener can no longer recognise those blocks as plugin-placed on the next start, so leftover fire behaves as vanilla fire and can spread and burn player structures. Was Gangland WP-38.

title: GunAction refunds a hardcoded 1 round on a cancelled WeaponShootEvent regardless of Consumed_Amount
fix: Refund weapon.getProjectileData().getConsumed() instead of the literal 1
observation: `boolean consumed = weapon.consumeShot();` subtracts projectileData.getConsumed() rounds via GunWeapon.consumeShot(), but the cancellation branch is `if (shootEvent.isCancelled()) { weapon.addAmmunition(1); return; }`. For any weapon configured with Consumed_Amount greater than 1, a plugin that cancels WeaponShootEvent leaves the shooter with fewer rounds than before the shot that never happened, destroying ammo on every cancelled press. Was Gangland WP-12.

title: Durability_On_Shot is silently ignored for biological, melee and throwable weapons
fix: Call weapon.decreaseDurability(heldWeapon, onShot) in BiologicalAction, MeleeAction and ThrowableAction as GunAction and IncendiaryAction do, or drop the key from those weapon types' YAML
tests: WeaponConsumeShotTest (javadoc cites the weapons.md divergence table, Observation #42)
observation: GunAction.java:71-74 and IncendiaryAction.java:99-101 both read `weapon.getDurabilityData().getOnShot()` and call decreaseDurability; a repo-wide grep shows those are the only two call sites. BiologicalAction.fire() and MeleeAction.activate() never call it, so a Durability_On_Shot configured on a biological or melee weapon never wears the item and those weapons never break. Separately only GunAction fires a cancellable WeaponShootEvent before the shot, so a protection plugin can veto gun fire but not incendiary, biological, melee or throwable fire. Was Gangland WP-42.

title: BiologicalAction action bar emits literal section-sign colour codes instead of the &-code convention
fix: Replace the literal section signs with &6/&e and route through BartizanChatUtil.color()
observation: The charge tick sends `ActionBarManager.send(player, "§6Charging... §e[" + "■".repeat(charge[0]) + ...)` with literal section-sign bytes in the source, while the release message two dozen lines later in the same class correctly uses &-codes (`"&aReleased at charge level " + level`). CLAUDE.md states colored chat must use &-codes through the ChatUtil path and never a literal section sign in source files. Was Gangland WP-27.

title: ThrowableAction.detonateStun plays a raw Sound enum constant instead of resolving through SoundEffect
fix: Replace the raw Sound.ENTITY_GENERIC_EXPLODE with a SoundEffect/XSound-resolved call
observation: detonateStun() calls `world.playSound(center, Sound.ENTITY_GENERIC_EXPLODE, 2.0f, 1.8f);` against the raw Bukkit Sound enum, while activate() and detonate() in the same file use SoundEffect.playSounds(...). CLAUDE.md requires version-drifting enums (Sound, Material, Particle, PotionEffectType) to resolve through XSeries so they survive a Minecraft version rename. Was Gangland WP-28.

title: BiologicalAction.fire never persists the magazine after consumeShot, so biological ammo is restored on the next interaction
fix: Call weapon.updateWeaponData(heldWeapon) and weapon.updateWeapon(player, heldWeapon, slot) after consumeShot, as GunAction and IncendiaryAction do
tests: WeaponConsumeShotTest (pins the in-memory decrement only, not the NBT write-back)
observation: fire() decrements the magazine with `if (!weapon.consumeShot()) return;` and then does nothing to write that state onto the item — a grep of the whole class for updateWeapon, heldWeapon, AMMO_LEFT and updateTag returns no hits, while GunAction.java:68,76 and IncendiaryAction.java:97,104 both call updateWeaponData followed by updateWeapon. Weapon.updateWeaponData is what stamps the tag, via `if (!updatedCurrentAmmo) updateTag(itemBuilder, WeaponTag.AMMO_LEFT, getAmmoLeftForTag());` at Weapon.java:249. On the next interaction WeaponService.validateAndGetWeapon resyncs from the held item and setWeaponData runs `weapon.setCurrentMagCapacity(amountLeft)` off the stale NBT, discarding the decrement and refilling the magazine. A biological weapon therefore never runs out of ammo across interactions no matter how many charged shots are fired. Was Gangland WP-14 (biological ammo NBT half).

title: WearableEquipListener only sees InventoryClickEvent, so right-click and hotbar-swap equip bypass the wearable permission
fix: Add a PlayerInteractEvent handler for right-click equip, add HOTBAR_SWAP to the recognised armor-slot actions, and cover BlockDispenseArmorEvent
observation: The class declares exactly one handler, `onArmorEquip(InventoryClickEvent event)`, and resolveArmorBeingEquipped only returns an item for an ARMOR-slot click whose action is `PLACE_ALL || PLACE_ONE || PLACE_SOME || SWAP_WITH_CURSOR`, or for a shift-click; every other case hits `return null;`. Right-clicking an armor piece held in hand — the ordinary vanilla way to equip armor — fires PlayerInteractEvent and never an InventoryClickEvent, and pressing a hotbar number key over an armor slot produces action HOTBAR_SWAP, which the whitelist omits. Neither path ever reaches `if (permission != null && !permission.isEmpty() && !player.hasPermission(permission))`, so any player can wear a permission-gated wearable by right-clicking it on, defeating bartizan.wearables.<key> entirely.

title: WearableAddon accepts any Traits key without validating it against TRAIT_TABLE, so a typo silently grants nothing
fix: Validate each Traits key against Wearable's TRAIT_TABLE during load and log.warn on an unmapped key
observation: The loader walks the Traits section and stores every key unconditionally with `traits.put(traitKey.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT), level);`, with no check against the TRAIT_TABLE declared at Wearable.java:55. Wearable.traitBonus then does `double[] definition = TRAIT_TABLE.get(key); if (definition == null) return 0;`, so a misspelling such as REINFORCE instead of REINFORCED loads cleanly and contributes exactly zero protection. The same method logs warnings for a bad Material or Name a few lines earlier, so the silence here is a divergence rather than a house style, and the admin gets a wearable that looks configured but does nothing.

title: WearableEquipListener's javadoc documents drop-cancellation for non-droppable wearables that is not implemented
fix: Delete the stale javadoc paragraph, or implement a PlayerDropItemEvent handler behind a real droppable flag
observation:
The class javadoc states `

On drop: if the wearable is marked as non-droppable the drop event is cancelled.` but the class declares only the single InventoryClickEvent handler. A case-insensitive grep for droppable and PlayerDropItemEvent across the wearable package, the api wearable package and wearables.yml returns nothing at all, so neither the flag nor the handler exists. The documented drop protection has never run in Bartizan and every wearable can be dropped freely.

title: The wearable permission-denied message is a hardcoded English string sent through Keystone ChatUtil, not BartizanMessages
fix: Add the string to BartizanMessages and message_en.yml and send it through BartizanChatUtil like the rest of the plugin
observation: The denial path sends `player.sendMessage(ChatUtil.color("&cYou are not authorized to equip this armor."));` using the raw Keystone `org.luckyraven.keystone.util.ChatUtil` import. Every other user-facing string in the plugin resolves through the BartizanMessages enum backed by message/message_en.yml and is sent via BartizanChatUtil, which also applies the money-symbol substitution. This string is therefore untranslatable on a non-English server and is the only wearable message not present in message_en.yml.

title: Wearable.buildItem stamps wt_ trait and wr_base NBT tags that nothing ever reads back
fix: Drop the per-trait and base-reduction stamps from buildItem, since every consumer resolves live values from the registry by NBT_KEY
observation: buildItem writes `builder.addTag(NBT_BASE_REDUCE, baseDamageReduction);` and, per trait, `builder.addTag(NBT_TRAIT_PREFIX + entry.getKey(), entry.getValue());`. A repo-wide grep for NBT_TRAIT_PREFIX and NBT_BASE_REDUCE finds only their declarations and these two write sites — no reader anywhere. WearableItemSerializer, WearableRefresher and BartizanItemPredicates all key exclusively off NBT_KEY and look the rest up live in the registry. The stamped values are write-only data that silently diverges from wearables.yml the moment an admin edits a trait, with no consumer on either side.

title: WearableRefresher.canRefresh claims any wearable-tagged ItemStack, but WearableService.getWearable can miss for a foreign or stale tag - the refresh silently falls through instead of refreshing or reporting an error
fix: canRefresh should distinguish "no wearable tag at all" (correctly not its concern) from "has a wearable tag WearableService doesn't recognise" (arguably worth a diagnostic/fault report instead of silent pass-through) - needs a Bartizan-side design decision, not a one-line fix; filed as triage, not a ready-to-fix row
observation: canRefresh only rejects a source with no wearable NBT tag at all (!hasNBTTag(Wearable.NBT_KEY) -> false); once the tag is present it returns true even when wearableService.getWearable(key) misses (unregistered/foreign/stale tag), relying on refresh() below to no-op safely (if (wearable == null) return null;, and ItemRefresherRegistry.java:62-70 falls through cleanly rather than throwing) - currently safe, not a crash, but a silent no-op with no diagnostic. As of the WS7 gadget wave (0.9.2/0.4.0) the method also carries a WS7-D4 comment and an !wearable.isExternal() exclusion for the jetpack's external-wearable registration, added for an unrelated reason but touching the same lines. Found WS7 G0-G1 review (this wave's setup gate), recorded as docket candidate (a); pre-existing, not introduced by and not itself touched by any WS7 gate.

title: An externally-registered Wearable (WearableCatalog.register) has getPermission() return null by design, meaning none of Bartizan's own wearable-permission-check machinery ever applies to it
fix: None needed for the jetpack specifically (already covered by Gangland's own Jetpack.getPermission() check in JetpackService.activate); worth a documentation note in bartizan-api.md's "External wearable registration" section (already present, confirmed during this gate) - this row exists mainly to make the relationship to Gangland docket GD-07 explicit and searchable, not to request a code change
observation: An externally-registered wearable (the mechanism Gangland's jetpack uses to keep its Bartizan-hosted armour traits since 0.9.2/0.4.0, see documentation/migration-0.9.2.md 3) is damage-only: never built, converted, given, listed or serialised by Bartizan, and getPermission() returns null unconditionally, so an external registrant gets no permission-node enforcement from Bartizan's side at all - by design, since Bartizan never builds/gives it and never runs its own equip-permission path for it. Cross-referenced against Gangland's open GD-07 ("the wearable permission is only checked on inventory clicks"), which is about Bartizan-native wearables' permission check being incomplete - a different case entirely from an external registrant having no Bartizan-side check at all. Found WS7 G0-G1 review, recorded as docket candidate (b).

title: Weapon block breaking calls block.setType(AIR) without ever firing BlockBreakEvent, bypassing every protection plugin
fix: Fire a cancellable BlockBreakEvent (or the region-plugin equivalent) in BlockDamageManager before removing the block and honour its cancellation
observation: BlockDamageManager removes blocks with a bare `block.setType(Material.AIR);` at two sites, reached from WeaponRaytracerImpl.applyBlockBreak (line 500-508) on every raytraced block hit that matches a Break_Blocks modifier. A repo-wide grep for BlockBreakEvent finds only an import and a listener in WeaponInteract — nothing in the plugin ever fires one. Five shipped weapons configure Break_Blocks (rifle ships `- GLASS-3`, `- ICE-5`, `- TERRACOTTA-10`, plus shotgun, minigun, steyr_aug, golden_ak47), so out of the box any player holding a rifle can destroy glass, ice and terracotta inside a WorldGuard or GriefPrevention claim with no plugin able to observe or veto it.

title: Cosmetic ROCKET Fireball is spawned without setYield(0), so vanilla explosion physics fire alongside the configured blast
fix: Call setYield(0f) and setIsIncendiary(false) on the spawned projectile inside WeaponVisualSpawner.spawnCosmetic
observation: WeaponShooting.fireSlow picks `Class<? extends Projectile> visualClass = type == ProjectileType.ROCKET ? Fireball.class : Firework.class;` and spawnCosmetic does only `projectile.setSilent(true); projectile.setGravity(false); projectile.setShooter(shooter); projectile.setVelocity(velocity);` before returning. A grep for setYield, setIsIncendiary, EntityExplodeEvent and ExplosionPrimeEvent across both modules returns nothing, so the Fireball keeps its default yield and explodes on contact through vanilla physics with real block destruction and entity damage. That fires in addition to SteppedProjectileTask's own configured fireExplosion, so every rocket shot produces one uncontrolled vanilla explosion that ignores Explosion_Radius and Explosion_Damage entirely, contradicting the spawner's javadoc that cosmetic entities never drive damage logic.

title: CombatEligibility.canBeHit is never consulted for the entity being shot, only for the shooter and reloader
fix: Gate the raytracer's entity filter on CombatEligibility.resolve().canBeHit(player) for Player targets, in WeaponShooting or as the RaytraceRequest default
observation: advanceRay's entity predicate is `e -> e != shooter && !(e instanceof ItemFrame || e instanceof ArmorStand) && request.getEntityFilter().test(e)`, and RaytraceRequest.Builder defaults `entityFilter = e -> true` (RaytraceRequest.java:69), which WeaponShooting never overrides. All six canBeHit call sites in the repo gate the acting player: WeaponInteract.java:147 and :224 gate the shooter, InstantReload and NumberedReload gate the reloader, and WiringConfig.java:162 only builds the holder bean. CombatEligibility's javadoc says it replaces Gangland's DownedPlayerRegistry and returns false for a player who is downed or otherwise protected, so the contract's primary purpose — making those players un-shootable — is not implemented on the damage path.

title: handleEntityImpact calls setInvulnerable(false) on every hit target and never restores the previous flag
fix: Capture living.isInvulnerable() before the call and restore it after damage is applied
observation: The default damage branch runs `living.setNoDamageTicks(0); living.setInvulnerable(false);` unconditionally before `living.damage(event.getDamage(), shooter)`, and nothing later in the method restores the flag. Any entity that was deliberately invulnerable — an admin in god mode, a spawn-protected mob, an NPC inside a plugin-driven invulnerability window — has that flag permanently cleared the first time a weapon shot touches it, long after the shot resolves. Was Gangland WP-22.

title: SteppedProjectileTask and its cosmetic entity leak on plugin disable, leaving orphaned visuals in the world
fix: Track live SteppedProjectileTask instances and call terminate() on each from a BeanLifecycle shutdown hook
observation: WeaponShooting constructs the task fire-and-forget as `new SteppedProjectileTask(...).start()` with no registry holding a reference. start() schedules a Keystone RepeatingTimer through runTaskTimer, and Bukkit cancels that BukkitTask on disable, but cancelling the tick callback never invokes terminate(), which is what removes the cosmetic Fireball/Firework and unregisters its id from WeaponVisualSpawner.cosmeticEntityIds. A rocket in flight during a reload or shutdown therefore leaves a permanent gravity-free projectile entity in the world with no owner to despawn it.

title: BlockDamageManager's delayed regeneration tasks throw on Objects.requireNonNull(location.getWorld()) after a world unload
fix: Null-check location.getWorld() in sendBlockDamage and clearBlockDamage and abandon the block instead of throwing
observation: Both sendBlockDamage (line 131) and clearBlockDamage (line 142) open with `World world = Objects.requireNonNull(location.getWorld());`. They are invoked from scheduleRegeneration, startSmoothRegeneration and breakAndScheduleRestore, all of which are Bukkit delayed or repeating tasks that can fire after the block's world has unloaded, and this repo's own house rule states Bukkit getWorld() is nullable and must be checked before use. Unloading a world with a weapon-cracked block mid-regeneration throws an uncaught NPE inside the scheduler callback, aborting that block's cleanup and leaving a stale damagedBlocks entry with a permanent crack overlay.

title: WeaponKillEntityEvent is declared in bartizan-api but never constructed or fired anywhere
fix: Fire it from handleEntityImpact when living.isDead() becomes true after damage, or delete the dead event class
observation: handleEntityImpact applies `living.damage(event.getDamage(), shooter)` and never re-checks isDead() to signal a kill. A repo-wide grep for WeaponKillEntityEvent returns only its own class file and constructor, with no callEvent site in either module, so the event is a dead public API a consumer plugin can register a listener for and never receive. WeaponEntityDamageEvent, the other half of the original pairing, is now genuinely fired from ThrowableAction, so only the kill event remains dead. Was Gangland WP-18, half-fixed.

title: Hitscan rays start at the shooter's eye while the rendered tracer starts at the muzzle offset
fix: Draw the tracer from the same origin the ray uses, or raytrace from WeaponMuzzle.compute consistently
observation: WeaponShooting.fireHitscan builds the request with `Location origin = shooter.getEyeLocation();` while drawTracerLine seeds `Location previous = WeaponMuzzle.compute(ctx.getRequest().getShooter(), ctx.getRequest().getDirection());` before walking the segments. The first rendered leg therefore runs from the muzzle offset (right of the body, below the eye) to the first real ray point, producing a visible kink that does not match the path the shot actually took. The same split exists in fireSlow, which spawns the visual at the muzzle but raytraces from the eye. Was Gangland WP-26.

title: BlockGroupResolver.resolve falls back to raw Material.valueOf instead of XMaterial
fix: Resolve names through XMaterial.matchXMaterial(...).map(XMaterial::parseMaterial)
observation: The single-material fallback is `try { Material material = Material.valueOf(upperName); return Set.of(material); } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) { return Collections.emptySet(); }`. CLAUDE.md requires version-drifting enums to resolve through XSeries and never raw valueOf, so a material renamed between Minecraft versions in a weapon's Break_Blocks list silently resolves to an empty set and that block group stops breaking, with no warning to the admin.

title: SteppedProjectileTask plays the explosion sound through the raw Sound enum instead of SoundEffect
fix: Route the call through org.luckyraven.keystone.sound.SoundEffect as WeaponRaytracerImpl already does
observation: The explosion effect plays `world.playSound(loc, Sound.ENTITY_GENERIC_EXPLODE, 2.0f, 1.0f);` against the raw Bukkit Sound enum, which CLAUDE.md bans in favour of XSeries-backed SoundEffect. The surrounding lines of the same method already resolve particles correctly through XParticle.EXPLOSION/SMOKE/FLAME.get(), so this is the one version-fragile call in an otherwise convention-following block.

title: BlockDamageManager's break effect uses the raw Particle enum instead of XParticle
fix: Resolve the particle through XParticle to match the rest of the raytrace and block-damage code
observation: The break effect calls `world.spawnParticle(Particle.BLOCK, location.clone().add(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), 25, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.05, blockData);` with a raw org.bukkit.Particle constant. Particle constant names have drifted across Minecraft versions (BLOCK_CRACK to BLOCK), which is exactly why CLAUDE.md requires XParticle here, and both WeaponRaytracerImpl's tracer and SteppedProjectileTask's explosion already use XParticle.X.get().

title: PenetrationModifier.calculateDamage is dead code; the real reduction math lives in ProjectileState
fix: Delete calculateDamage, or wire it in and remove the duplicate logic in ProjectileState.applyPenetrationReduction
observation: `public double calculateDamage(double baseDamage, int penetrationCount) { return baseDamage * Math.pow(1.0 - damageReduction, penetrationCount); }` has no call site anywhere in either module. The per-hit reduction actually applied during a shot comes from ProjectileState.applyPenetrationReduction's cumulative multiplier, so this method is unreferenced modifier logic that duplicates, and could silently diverge from, the live formula.

title: WeaponLoader logs a weapon parse failure at log.info, burying a broken config in startup chatter
fix: Log the caught InvalidConfigurationException at log.warn or log.error
observation: The load callback is `try { weaponAddon.registerWeapon(ammunitionManager, fileHandler); } catch (InvalidConfigurationException exception) { log.info("There was a problem loading the weapon: {}", exception.getMessage()); }`. Every validation throw in the five weapon parsers — missing Selective_Fire, missing Projectile, missing Damage, an unresolvable Display_Item.Material — lands here and is reported at info level, indistinguishable from routine startup output. The weapon does correctly stay out of WeaponAddon's map so tab-completion no longer offers it, which is an improvement on the original Gangland report, but the admin gets no visible signal that a weapon silently vanished from the catalogue. Partially reproduces Gangland WP-31, log level only.

title: WeaponAddon.registerWeapon returns early and skips the entire file when a Config_Version key is present
fix: Log a warning and continue parsing, or implement the versioned-config handling the key implies
observation: registerWeapon opens with `String configVersion = root.get("Config_Version").asString().orNull(); if (configVersion != null) { return; }`, aborting before any section is parsed, before the ConfigReport is logged, and before the weapon is put into the catalogue map. Adding a `Config_Version:` key — an ordinary versioning habit for a config author — therefore makes the weapon disappear with zero output anywhere. No shipped weapon YAML sets the key, so this is a live trap rather than a current break. Was Gangland WP-39.

title: GunWeaponParser defaults Shoot.Projectile.Consumed_Amount to 0, giving an omitted key an infinite magazine
fix: Change `.min(0).orDefault(0)` to `.min(1).orDefault(1)`
tests: WeaponConsumeShotTest (pins today's wrong behaviour; javadoc names Observation #13)
observation: The parser reads `int projectileConsumed = projectile.get("Consumed_Amount").asInt().min(0).orDefault(0);`, which flows into GunWeapon.consumeShot()'s `setCurrentMagCapacity(Math.max(0, getCurrentMagCapacity() - projectileData.getConsumed()));`. With the key omitted the subtraction is a no-op while consumeShot() still returns true, so the gun fires forever and never needs a reload. All 26 shipped weapon YAMLs set Consumed_Amount: 1, making this a latent trap for the next hand-authored gun rather than a default-config break. Was Gangland WP-13.

title: AmmunitionSectionParser accepts Capacity, Restore and a numbered-reload amount of 0, feeding division by zero in NumberedReload
fix: Enforce min(1) on Ammunition.Capacity and Restore and on the amount parsed out of a `numbered-N` Reload.Type
observation: `int capacity = ammo.get("Capacity").asInt().min(0).orDefault(0);` and `int restore = ammo.get("Restore").asInt().min(0).orDefault(capacity);` both permit 0, and the `typeAmount = Integer.parseInt(parts[1])` for a `Type: numbered-0` string is unvalidated. NumberedReload then divides by both: `int numberOfInsertions = leftToInsert / ammunitionData.getRestore();` and `int maxPossibleInsertions = numberOfAmmunition / amount;`. Either a zero Restore or a numbered-0 type throws ArithmeticException the moment a player reloads that weapon. Every shipped weapon uses instant reload, so this is currently unreachable but crashes immediately once someone authors a numbered one. Was Gangland WP-11.

title: BiologicalWeaponParser never validates that Effects_Per_Level is non-empty, unlike ThrowableWeaponParser's STUN check
fix: Throw InvalidConfigurationException when Effects_Per_Level is empty, mirroring the sibling parser's guard
observation: The parser reads `List<String> effectsPerLevel = shoot.get("Effects_Per_Level").asList().ofStrings().orEmpty();` with no emptiness check, while ThrowableWeaponParser explicitly guards its analogous list with `if (type == ThrowableType.STUN && effects.isEmpty()) { throw new InvalidConfigurationException(...); }` — a direct divergence between two structurally similar parsers. Downstream, BiologicalAction.java:115-116 indexes `data.getEffectsPerLevel().get(Math.min(level, data.getEffectsPerLevel().size()) - 1)`, which is get(-1) for an empty list and throws IndexOutOfBoundsException after ammo, sound and recoil have already been applied. The shipped syringe_gun.yml supplies three entries, so this is latent until someone authors a biological weapon without the key. Was Gangland WP-15.

title: An unknown Category and an unresolvable Material silently fall back to OTHER, FEATHER and IRON_PICKAXE with no warning
fix: Emit a ConfigReport warning whenever WeaponType.getType or XMaterial.matchXMaterial falls through to its default
observation: `WeaponType category = WeaponType.getType(Objects.requireNonNull(categoryString));` resolves any typo'd Category through WeaponType.getType's `default -> OTHER;`, which silently routes the weapon into GunWeaponParser because that parser handles `case GUN, OTHER ->`. The same block falls back to `material = XMaterial.FEATHER.get();` when the Material string does not resolve, and AmmunitionAddon.java:77-79 does the analogous `xMaterialOptional.orElse(XMaterial.IRON_PICKAXE)`. A weapon with a misspelled category or material therefore loads as a subtly wrong item with no diagnostic at all. Was Gangland WP-30.

title: MeleeWeaponParser never calls setAllowedSelectiveFires, so melee weapons cycle to AUTO and BURST despite Selective_Fire single
fix: Set weapon.setAllowedSelectiveFires(EnumSet.of(SelectiveFire.SINGLE)) in MeleeWeaponParser as the other parsers do
observation: parse() builds and returns a MeleeWeapon without ever calling setAllowedSelectiveFires, while GunWeaponParser.java:117, BiologicalWeaponParser.java:55-58 and IncendiaryWeaponParser.java:53-56 all set it and fall back to an explicit single-mode EnumSet. Weapon.allowedSelectiveFires has no default and stays null, and SelectiveFire.getNextState(Set) opens with `if (allowed == null || allowed.isEmpty()) return getNextState();` — documented as no restriction. crowbar.yml, knife.yml and machete.yml all configure Selective_Fire: single, yet a normal sneak plus swap-hand cycles them through AUTO and BURST. Melee firing behaviour is unaffected because WeaponInteract only reads the mode off gun and incendiary typed variables, so the damage is a wrong mode shown in the action bar, in /bartizan weapon info and in the item's SELECTIVE_FIRE NBT tag.

title: BartizanSettings.init throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and aborts plugin boot when Money_Symbol is set to an empty string
fix: Fall back to the default when the configured Money_Symbol is blank, before calling substring
observation: init() runs `moneySymbol = str(root, "Money_Symbol", "$").substring(0, 1);` and the str() helper is `if (parent == null) return def; return parent.get(key).asString().orDefault(def);` — the default only substitutes for an absent key, so an explicitly configured `Money_Symbol: ""` returns the empty string and substring(0, 1) throws. This runs inside a FILE-phase bean initializer, so the exception aborts the whole bean-instantiation pipeline and the plugin fails to enable rather than degrading one feature. Confidence is Medium only because it depends on Keystone's orDefault treating an explicit empty value as present rather than absent.

title: WeaponAddon accepts Durability.Base of 0, producing a NaN durability scale that silently truncates to 0
fix: Require Durability.Base of at least 1 with min(1) in WeaponAddon so the downstream divisions cannot degrade
observation: `durability = (short) dur.get("Base").asInt().min(0).required().orDefault(0);` permits 0. Two independent consumers then divide by it with no guard: Weapon.buildItem() at Weapon.java:207-208 computes `(durability - currentDurability) * (builder.getItemMaxDurability() / (double) durability)`, and DurabilityCalculator.getWeaponDurability computes `double scale = itemMaxDurability / weaponMaxDurability;`. Both yield NaN or Infinity, and the narrowing cast to short silently gives 0, so the item renders at full durability instead of surfacing the misconfiguration. Validating once at parse time fixes both call sites. Was Gangland WP-33.

title: The flare entry in ammunition.yml is dead — no shipped weapon references that ammo type
fix: Delete the unused flare entry, or add the flare-firing weapon it was written for
observation: The catalogue defines `flare:` with `Material: "SUGAR"` and `Name: "&cFlare&r"` alongside 9mm, 7,62, 5,56, rocket, 50_bmg, slugs, fuel_canister and pathogen_vial. Grepping the Ammo_Type key across every shipped weapon YAML shows only 9mm, 7,62, 5,56, pathogen_vial, fuel_canister, rocket and slugs are ever referenced, so flare can never be consumed or handed to a player through any weapon's reload path. Was Gangland WP-41.

title: WeaponRepository.deleteAll wraps a backend call in an unused legacy Database and bypasses Diagnostics routing
fix: Route deleteAll through AbstractRepository's own backend-async path so failures reach reportBackendFailure like save, saveAll and delete
observation: The whole method is `DatabaseHelper helper = new DatabaseHelper(getPlugin(), getDatabaseHandler()); helper.runQueriesAsync(database -> tableBackend().delete(null));` — the lambda ignores the injected legacy `database` parameter entirely and calls tableBackend(), the HikariCP DatabaseBackend path, so DatabaseHelper's synchronized block and connect/disconnect bracketing guard nothing that is actually used. DatabaseHelper.runQueries opens with `if (database == null) return;`, so a null legacy handle makes the entire table delete a silent no-op with no logging. Any SQLException from the backend delete is swallowed by DatabaseHelper's generic warn and never reaches Diagnostics.active(), unlike every other mutation path in AbstractRepository.

title: doLoadAll calls UUID.fromString per row, so one malformed uuid aborts the entire repository load
fix: Wrap the per-row parse in try/catch, log the bad row through Diagnostics and skip it
observation: The load loop runs `UUID uuid = UUID.fromString(String.valueOf(result[0]));` for every row returned by tableBackend().selectAll(). UUID.fromString throws an unchecked IllegalArgumentException, while doLoadAll is declared `throws SQLException` and AbstractRepository.loadAll catches only SQLException around it. A single corrupted uuid cell — from a partial write, a manual edit or a migration artifact — therefore propagates uncaught out of WeaponManager.initialize() and aborts the whole weapon load rather than costing one row.

title: doLoadAll silently discards every row whose weapon type left the catalogue, and returns empty if weaponAddon is unset
fix: Log a warning naming the uuid and type when the template is missing, and treat an unset weaponAddon as an error rather than an empty result
observation: The loop contains `if (weaponAddon == null) continue;` and `if (template == null) continue;` with no logging in either branch. Renaming or deleting a weapon YAML makes every persisted row of that type silently vanish on every subsequent load, with no signal that stored weapon identities were dropped. Worse, if weaponAddon has not been wired at the moment loadAll runs, the first guard fires for every row and the method returns an empty collection for the entire table, which is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty database.

title: WeaponDataCleanupTask wipes the entire weapon table on a blind timer instead of scoping to orphaned rows
fix: Scope the delete to rows no longer backing any live weapon item, rather than an unconditional full-table DELETE
tests: WeaponDataCleanupTaskTest (mocks the repository, so it pins call order only, not the real table consequence)
observation: cleanup() unconditionally runs `repo.deleteAll()` followed by `weaponManager.clear()`, deleting every persisted uuid and type row and every cached Weapon for the whole server on the Clean_Up.Time schedule, which settings.yml ships at 30 days. There is no WHERE clause and no staleness test, so weapons players are actively carrying are wiped alongside genuinely dead rows. The blast radius is bounded rather than catastrophic because WeaponService re-mints an instance under the item's own uuid and resyncs ammo, durability and fire mode from the item's NBT on next interaction, but every untouched weapon loses its database identity until someone handles it, and DebugCommand reports a population of zero straight after each wipe. The related in-memory leak this wipe is currently the only bound on is filed separately as BZ-WM-04.

title: WeaponTableImportTask only looks for a legacy SQLite file, so a MySQL Gangland install is skipped and marked done
fix: Detect Database.Type mysql and either import from that schema or log at warn that a manual migration is required, before writing the marker
tests: WeaponTableImportTaskTest (covers the file-absent and SQLException cases, never a MySQL source)
observation: The one-shot import resolves `File ganglandDatabase = new File(bartizan.getDataFolder().getParentFile(), "Gangland_Warfare" + File.separator + "database" + File.separator + "gangland.db");` and, when absent, logs at debug that this is "a fresh install or a MySQL deployment, not an error" and calls writeMarker(marker) before returning. A Gangland server running Database.Type mysql never has that file, so the branch always fires, the message is invisible because Debug.Enable defaults to false, and the marker permanently records the import as complete. The migration opportunity is silently and irreversibly lost with no admin-facing message and no retry path.

title: The three give commands never bound the parsed amount, so a negative throws and a zero reports a false success
fix: Clamp the parsed amount to at least 1 and to a sane maximum right after Integer.parseInt, in all three give commands
