observation: giveWeapon takes the amount straight from `weaponAmount = Integer.parseInt(args[3])` with no range check and computes `int slots = (int) Math.ceil(amount / (double) maxStackSize);` then `ItemStack[] items = new ItemStack[slots];`. For an amount of -100 against a stack size of 64, slots is -1 and `new ItemStack[-1]` throws NegativeArraySizeException, which the command framework surfaces to the admin as a bare number. For an amount of 0 the array is empty, the loop never runs, and giveWeapon still returns true, so the admin is told the give succeeded while nothing entered the inventory. A very large amount drives an unbounded allocation instead. The identical pattern is duplicated in AmmunitionGiveCommand.java:91-104 and WearableGiveCommand.java:96-108.

title: The weapon alias on /bartizan shadows WeaponCommand's own subcommand label, so /weapon give never dispatches
fix: Remove weapon from plugin.yml's aliases list for the bartizan command, keeping btz
observation: plugin.yml registers a single Bukkit command, bartizan, with `aliases: [btz, weapon]`, while WeaponCommand registers weapon as one of its own subcommand labels alongside ammo, wearable, debug and reload. Typing `/weapon give ak47 5` makes Bukkit consume weapon as the invoking alias and hand the dispatcher args[0]="give", which matches no registered subcommand, so the sender gets an unknown-subcommand error with a did-you-mean suggestion. Only `/bartizan weapon give ...` and `/btz weapon give ...` reach WeaponGiveCommand, leaving the weapon alias useful only for the bare `/weapon` info card.

title: WeaponGiveCommand tab-completes from weaponLoader.getFiles(), offering weapon files that failed to parse
fix: Source the name completion from weaponAddon.getWeaponKeys() as WeaponInfoCommand and WeaponListCommand already do
observation: The name argument's completion supplier is `return weaponLoader.getFiles().stream().map(FileHandler::getName).toList();`, which lists every YAML physically present in the weapon folder whether or not it registered a Weapon. WeaponInfoCommand and WeaponListCommand instead use weaponAddon.getWeaponKeys(), which holds only successfully parsed weapons. A weapon whose config failed to load is therefore still offered in `/bartizan weapon give <tab>`, and picking it makes getWeapon return null so the admin gets INVALID_WEAPON instead of an item. AmmunitionGiveCommand and WearableGiveCommand do not share the divergence. Was Gangland WP-31.

title: The three WEARABLE error messages use Type.PREFIX while the weapon and ammo equivalents use Type.ERROR
fix: Change WEARABLE_INVALID, WEARABLE_NOT_REGISTERED and WEARABLE_NOT_WEARABLE to Type.ERROR
observation: The enum declares `WEARABLE_INVALID("Errors.Wearable.Invalid", Type.PREFIX)` plus the same for WEARABLE_NOT_REGISTERED and WEARABLE_NOT_WEARABLE, while the sibling failures are `INVALID_WEAPON("Errors.Not_Valid_Weapon", Type.ERROR)` and `INVALID_AMMO("Errors.Not_Valid_Ammo", Type.ERROR)`. Type.PREFIX renders through the generic plugin prefix rather than the red Errors.Prefix, so a wrong wearable name, an unregistered key or a non-wearable item reads as ordinary informational chat instead of an error, inconsistent with the identical weapon and ammo paths in the same command package.

title: WeaponInteract's eight per-weapon state maps are never cleared on player quit, leaving timers running for an offline player
fix: Extend WeaponQuitCleanupListener to stop and remove the quitting player's entries in autoTasks, activeTasks, continuousFire, pressHoldState and the rest
observation: WeaponInteract owns continuousFire, pressLockUntilTick, pressHoldState, releaseCallbacks, autoTasks, activeTasks, meleeCooldowns and lastMeleeSwingMs, all keyed by weapon UUID and all cleared only from onWeaponHeld on a weapon swap. WeaponQuitCleanupListener.onPlayerQuit reads only `ItemStack item = player.getInventory().getItemInMainHand();` and then calls stopReloading() and unScope(player, true), touching none of the maps. A player who disconnects mid-AUTO-fire or mid-throwable-charge leaves the FullAutoTask and RepeatingTimer entries running and calling Bukkit Player APIs against an offline Player until their own watchdog eventually times out. Was Gangland WP-9, quit path.

title: Async press-hold watchdogs write the non-volatile WeaponData.shooting flag the main-thread interact handler also writes
fix: Run these watchdogs with start(false) as handleBiologicalCharge already does, or make WeaponData.shooting an AtomicBoolean
observation: engagePressHoldWatchdog and shootFullAuto's AUTO watchdog both schedule a RepeatingTimer with `.start(true)` under the comment "Pure flag-flipping + map mutation, so safe to run async", and mutate `stillHeld.get().shooting = false;`. WeaponData declares `private boolean shooting;` with no volatile, and the same field is set true from the main thread at lines 396, 478, 527 and 653 during PlayerInteractEvent handling. The eight surrounding maps are all ConcurrentHashMap so there is no map corruption, but the flag itself has no memory barrier, so a release can be missed for a cycle and the press-lock either lingers or re-arms late. shootFullAuto's async watchdog additionally calls resetRecoilPattern(), mutating RecoilManager.playerPatternIndex concurrently with applyRecoil on the main thread.

title: The scope-toggle branch swallows a non-sneaking left click on every weapon that has no scope configured
fix: Enter the scope branch only when scopeData is not null, instead of defaulting validateScope to true
observation: onPlayerInteract computes `boolean validateScope = true; if (scopeData != null) { validateScope = scopeData.getLevel() > 0; }`, so a weapon with no ScopeData keeps validateScope true and enters `if (leftClick && !player.isSneaking() && validateScope && !weapon.isReloading())`. That branch denies the interaction, calls unScope, plays the scope sound and `return`s before execution can reach handleNonGunInteract's melee branch below. A scope-less melee weapon swung at air or a block with a plain left click therefore never reaches MeleeAction; only sneak-left-click does, though entity hits still land through the separate damage handler. Was Gangland WP-5.

title: WeaponService.getWeaponUUID calls UUID.fromString on raw NBT with no try/catch, throwing out of every listener
fix: Wrap the parse in try/catch, log at warn and return null on IllegalArgumentException
observation: getWeaponUUID reads the tag with `String stringTagData = tempItem.getStringTagData(tagProperName);` and then does `if (!(value == null || value.equals("null") || value.isEmpty())) { uuid = UUID.fromString(value); }` with no guard. This is the first thing every listener in the system reaches through validateAndGetWeapon — WeaponInteract, WeaponDroppedListener, WeaponItemSpawnListener, WeaponQuitCleanupListener, WeaponReloadListener and WeaponSelectiveFireChangeListener all route through it. A hand-edited or corrupted UUID tag throws IllegalArgumentException out of the @EventHandler method for all of them, and because the item stays in the inventory the exception repeats on every interaction. Was Gangland WP-24.

title: WeaponQuitCleanupListener inspects only the main hand, so an off-hand weapon's reload and scope state survives the disconnect
fix: Check OFF_HAND as well, mirroring WeaponService.getHeldWeaponItem's own main-then-offhand fallback
observation: onPlayerQuit does `ItemStack item = player.getInventory().getItemInMainHand(); Weapon weapon = weaponManager.validateAndGetWeapon(player, item); if (weapon == null) return;` and never looks at getItemInOffHand(). WeaponService.getHeldWeaponItem explicitly falls back to EquipmentSlot.OFF_HAND when the main hand is not a weapon, and WeaponSelectiveFireChangeListener depends on that fallback, so off-hand weapons are a supported case. A player quitting while reloading or scoped with an off-hand weapon leaves the reloading and scoped flags stuck on that weapon instance.

title: shootInterval schedules a fresh Consume_On_Time CountdownTimer on every shot instead of restarting one
fix: Keep one timer per weapon and restart it, cancelling any previous timer before scheduling
observation: Whenever Consume_On_Time is configured above -1, shootInterval unconditionally builds `CountdownTimer timer = new CountdownTimer(plugin, 0L, 0L, consumeOnTime, null, null, time -> weapon.removeWeapon(player, player.getInventory().getHeldItemSlot()));` and starts it. Firing several shots before the first timer elapses stacks independent timers that each call removeWeapon on whatever item then occupies that hotbar slot, so a slot reused after the weapon is gone can have an unrelated item removed. Dormant in practice because no shipped weapon configures Consume_On_Time. Was Gangland WP-29.

title: shootOtherModes derives the SINGLE-mode press-lock window from Per_Shot, which only applies to BURST
fix: Compute lockTicks from the number of shots actually fired, which is 1 for SINGLE and perShot for BURST
observation: shootOtherModes serves both SINGLE and BURST and computes `long lockTicks = Math.max((long) projectileData.getPerShot() * projectileData.getCooldown(), MIN_PRESS_LOCK_TICKS);` unconditionally, while the shoot() call it then makes only fires perShot rounds when the mode is BURST and otherwise fires one. A weapon whose BURST mode is configured with Per_Shot above 1 therefore gets that inflated press-lock in SINGLE mode too, so single fire is slower than its configured cooldown implies. Was Gangland WP-35.

title: WeaponChangeSelectiveFireEvent declares getHandlerList() private, unlike all seven sibling event classes
fix: Make it public static to match the rest of the package and the Bukkit event contract
observation: The class declares `private static HandlerList getHandlerList() { return handler; }` while WeaponReloadEvent, WeaponEntityDamageEvent, WeaponRaytraceImpactEvent, WeaponReloadStartEvent, WeaponReloadCompleteEvent, WeaponShootEvent and WeaponKillEntityEvent all declare it public static. Registration itself still works, because Bukkit's SimplePluginManager resolves the handler list with getDeclaredMethod plus setAccessible(true) rather than getMethod — so this is not the registration break it first appears to be. The real cost is that this is a bartizan-api class meant for cross-plugin consumption and a consumer cannot call WeaponChangeSelectiveFireEvent.getHandlerList() to unregister, which every other event in the package permits.

title: Bartizan.onDisable calls the test-only PacketBridge.reset, wiping the server-global packet adapter every other Keystone plugin shares
fix: Remove the PacketBridge.reset() call from onDisable, or replace it with a scoped uninstall that only reverts an adapter Bartizan itself installed
observation: onDisable runs `getServer().getServicesManager().unregisterAll(this); PacketBridge.reset();` before tearing down the context. Keystone's PacketBridge holds `private static volatile PacketAdapter adapter = NoOpAdapter.INSTANCE;` — one server-global instance shared by every consumer plugin on the shared Keystone classloader — and its reset() carries the javadoc "Reset to the no-op fallback. Test-only." Disabling or reloading Bartizan therefore silently downgrades recoil and packet handling to a no-op for every other Keystone-powered plugin still running, with no log line. The same path also runs when bootstrap fails, since onEnable's catch calls disablePlugin(this).

title: Bartizan.dependencyHandler logs "Found X, linking" and "Linked X" while always passing a null Runnable
fix: Either pass the real linking Runnable for each soft dependency or drop the misleading linking log lines
observation: dependencyHandler calls `viaVersion.validate(null)`, `placeholderApi.validate(null)` and `nbtApi.validate(null)`, and Dependency.validate is `if (Bukkit.getPluginManager().getPlugin(name) == null) return; log.info("Found {}, linking...", name); if (runnable != null) runnable.run(); log.info("Linked {}", name);`. Since the Runnable is always null nothing is ever linked, yet the console reports a successful link for each plugin found. NBTAPI is additionally a hard `depend:` entry in plugin.yml, so Bukkit guarantees it is present before onEnable and routing it through a soft-dependency helper makes that branch permanently dead.

title: BartizanContext declares both a Lombok @Getter and a hand-written getContainer(), leaving one dead
fix: Delete the hand-written getContainer() and keep the @Getter, or drop the annotation
observation: The field is declared `@Getter private final DependencyContainer container;` while the class also defines `public DependencyContainer getContainer() { return container; }` at lines 179-181. Lombok skips generating an accessor when one already exists, so this compiles cleanly and behaves correctly, but one of the two declarations is dead and a reader cannot tell which accessor is authoritative or whether the annotation is load-bearing.

title: RequirementHook.evaluateMinimum dispatches onSuccess for every passing set, double-spending consumable gates
fix: Make evaluateMinimum stop dispatching success once `min` sets have passed (matching evaluateAny for min=1), or dispatch success to exactly the sets that were needed
tests: RequirementHookTest (exercises minimum=2 only, does not pin minimum=1 dispatch count)
observation: evaluateMinimum() evaluates all sets, then on a pass runs `for (RequirementSet set : passed) { set.dispatchSuccess(dispatchCtx); }` for every set that passed. evaluateAny() (RequirementHook.java:217-228) instead fires success for only the first passing set and returns, and the evaluateMinimum javadoc claims to be "the natural generalisation of evaluateAll (min = M) and evaluateAny (min = 1)" — so min=1 contradicts its own documented contract. `minimum_requirements: 1` is reachable from user YAML (RequirementParser.java:155-156 clamps with `.asInt().min(1)`) and is emitted directly by the DeluxeMenus importer (DeluxeMenusImporter.java:961-965, whose javadoc at line 906 shows `minimum_requirements: 1`). RequirementSet's javadoc calls onSuccess "load-bearing for consumable gates ... the cooldown is spent only" there, so an imported N-of-M gate where two alternative sets both pass spends both resources on a single click instead of one.

title: InMemoryMenuRegistry.openPrevious re-opens with empty args and aborts on a required argument_processor
fix: Retain the args a menu was opened with in NavigationHistory, or skip the required-chain abort when the open originates from back-navigation
observation: openPrevious() always re-opens the popped menu with no arguments: `return doOpen(player, previous.get(), new String[0]);`. doOpen() then looks up that menu's ArgumentProcessorSpec and, when a processor is required, the empty args fail the bind and it runs `spec.fireRequired(player, result); return false;` (InMemoryMenuRegistry.java:96-102). A `menu_back` click into any menu registered with a required `argument_processor:` therefore opens nothing and instead fires that menu's "you must supply X" fail chain through a HeadlessClickContext, out of context for a backward navigation. The inline comment at line 84 acknowledges args are dropped but not that the open can abort entirely.

title: NavigationHistory.back consumes the trail step even when the popped-to menu is no longer registered
fix: Have openPrevious push the step back onto the trail when doOpen returns false, or verify the name is still registered before removing it
tests: NavigationHistoryTest (covers normal pop order, not a since-unregistered target)
observation: back() unconditionally does `trail.removeLast(); return Optional.ofNullable(trail.peekLast());` with no check that the returned name still resolves. openPrevious() feeds that name straight into doOpen(), which returns false at `Supplier<Menu> factory = factories.get(name); if (factory == null) return false;` when the menu was dropped by MenuConfigService.reload() -> `registry.unregister(name)` (MenuConfigService.java:147); unregister() only clears `factories`/`argSpecs` and never touches any player's trail, and NavigationHistory.clear() is called only per-viewer from DefaultOpenMenuTracker.java:104. The player's back-navigation silently does nothing while the trail has already lost that step, so a second `menu_back` skips past the gap instead of retrying it.

title: ImportService.writeTree truncates an existing imported YAML with no existence check
fix: Check Files.exists(outFile) before writing and warn-and-skip or version-suffix on a collision, instead of silently truncating
observation: writeTree opens the destination with `Files.newBufferedWriter(outFile, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)`, whose default CREATE plus TRUNCATE_EXISTING semantics overwrite unconditionally, and no existence check precedes it. The per-menu loop at lines 126-133 resolves `outFile = menuOutDir.resolve(safeFileName(menu.name()) + ".yml")`. Re-running /menu import therefore discards any hand-edits an admin made to a previously imported file under menus/imported/<source>/ with no warning and no report entry. Worse, safeFileName collapses every non-alphanumeric character to an underscore, so two source menus named "Shop A" and "Shop-A" both resolve to shop_a and silently clobber each other inside a single import run — one imported menu is simply lost.

title: Four bundled demo menus are missing from MenuConfigService's addExpectedFile list and never reach a fresh install
fix: Add addExpectedFile entries for gangland_demo, item_requirement_demo, vault_economy_demo and vault_group_demo alongside the existing 25
observation: The constructor registers exactly 25 `addExpectedFile(new FileHandler(plugin, "<name>", MENUS_FOLDER, "yml"))` calls, which FolderLoader uses to seed plugins/Oriel/menus/ on a fresh install, but menu-plugin/src/main/resources/menus/ ships 29 yml files — I confirmed both counts directly. gangland_demo.yml, item_requirement_demo.yml, vault_economy_demo.yml and vault_group_demo.yml are absent from the list, and a repo-wide grep finds zero Java references to any of the four names. They ship inside the jar but are never extracted, so a fresh admin install can never see them — including both Vault demos, the only shipped examples of the economy and group integrations.

title: AnvilClickContext substitutes raw player-typed %input% into elevated op and permission command strings
fix: Refuse or escape a %input% token inside an elevated op/permission command string, and document the interaction in ActionParser's elevated-action javadoc
observation: The constructor wraps the placeholder provider so the anvil's typed text is substituted first: `String withInput = raw.contains("%input%") ? raw.replace("%input%", safeInput) : raw;`, where `String safeInput = input == null ? "" : input;` performs no sanitization at all — the surrounding comment shows "safe" means only that the input is not itself re-expanded as a placeholder. ActionParser.runElevated (ActionParser.java:648-673) resolves an op or permission action's command through `ctx.placeholders().resolve(player, command)` without distinguishing an anvil-fed context, so a menu author writing an anvil_input on_confirm of `op: "%input%"` lets the typing player dictate the literal command executed under temporary op. The temp-op and PermissionAttachment grants are themselves correctly revoked in finally blocks, and allow_elevated_actions defaults to false, which bounds this to a trusted-author footgun rather than an open hole — but nothing in the code or docs flags the combination.

title: give_slot validates only a lower bound and hands an out-of-range index to the live Bukkit inventory
fix: Validate give_slot against the menu's real slot count at parse time, mirroring SlotLoader's config.slot.range report
observation: give_slot is parsed with a lower bound only — `NodeReader.of(mapping, report).get("give_slot").asInt().min(0).required().orElse(-1)` — and guarded at runtime only for negatives via `if (slot < 0) return NO_OP;`. The click handler then calls `chest.bukkitInventory().getItem(slot)` with no upper-bound check. Every other slot-index path in this system validates against the menu's real size: SlotLoader.load reports config.slot.range and skips when `slot < 0 || slot >= size` (SlotLoader.java:56-60). An admin typo such as give_slot 99 in a one-row nine-slot chest therefore reaches the live inventory and throws out of the click handler instead of being caught as a config error at load time.

title: MenuConfigService.registerMenu never calls the factory, so ChestMenuBuilder.build validation is deferred to first open
fix: Invoke factory.get() once during registerMenu so build()'s IllegalStateExceptions surface as ConfigReport entries with file and field at reload time
observation: ChestMenuLoader returns a Supplier<Menu> whose lambda calls builder.build() fresh per open, by design so per-player state cannot leak. registerMenu only does `registry.register(name, factory);` and never calls factory.get(), so ChestMenuBuilder's own range checks — `if (slotIndex < 0 || slotIndex >= size) { throw new IllegalStateException("slot " + slotIndex + " out of range [0, " + size + ")"); }` at ChestMenuBuilder.java:314-315, plus the region row/col throws at lines 393 and 398 — never run during /menu reload. A malformed pagination button slot or region value passes reload with zero report entries and throws only when a player opens the menu, where InMemoryMenuRegistry.doOpen catches it generically and logs a warning carrying no file, line or field. That directly contradicts PLAN section 7's "Builder validation runs on .build(), not on first open. Fail early." Reload reports success while the menu is unopenable.

title: Paginated previous_button, next_button and search_button slots skip the upper-bound check SlotLoader enforces
fix: Validate those three slots against rows times 9 in parseSlotMaterial and parseSearchButton, mirroring SlotLoader's config.slot.range report
observation: parseSlotMaterial (used for paginated.previous_button and next_button) and parseSearchButton both read the slot with a lower bound only — `int slot = r.get("slot").asInt().min(0).required().orElse(-1);` at line 200 and the identical line at 484 — then guard only with `if (slot < 0 || matName.isEmpty()) return null;`. SlotLoader.load, which every menu type's main slots block routes through, instead reports config.slot.range and skips whenever `slot < 0 || slot >= size` (SlotLoader.java:56-60). A typo such as previous_button slot 999 in a three-row chest passes the loader silently and only surfaces through finding 5's deferred build, so three of the loader's own slot-reading call sites bypass the range convention the rest of the system follows.

title: ItemDefinitionWriter.isNamespacedReference misses dash-prefixed MaterialSource refs, so the editor flattens dynamic heads
fix: Extend isNamespacedReference to treat a registered MaterialSource dash prefix as dynamic, mirroring ItemDefinitionLoader's dash dispatch
tests: ItemDefinitionWriterRoundTripTest does not cover this case
observation: ItemDefinitionLoader resolves a scalar item value with a dash before any colon through the MaterialSourceRegistry — `MaterialSource source = dash > 0 && sourceRegistry != null ? sourceRegistry.lookup(itemRef.substring(0, dash)) : null;` (ItemDefinitionLoader.java:413-416) — so head-, basehead-, texture- and the soft-dep prefixes resolve per player at render time exactly as dynamically as a namespace:key reference. ItemDefinitionWriter.isNamespacedReference recognises only the colon form: `int colon = text.indexOf(':'); return colon > 0 && colon < text.length() - 1;`. A dash reference has no colon, so it returns false. When an admin drops a physical item into the in-game editor to reset a slot icon, writeInto sees neither animated nor namespaced and overwrites `item: head-%player_name%` with the resolved literal material, permanently destroying the per-player skin reference on save — the same loss the writer's javadoc says it avoids for the colon form.

title: RequirementParser.parseItem uses raw Material.matchMaterial instead of the house MaterialLookup convention
fix: Resolve the item requirement's material through MaterialLookup.parse so it matches every other material lookup in the system
observation: parseItem resolves the material with `Material material = Material.matchMaterial(materialName.trim());` and reports config.requirement.item.material when it returns null. Every other material lookup in this system — ChestMenuLoader's slot buttons, ItemDefinitionLoader, TraderMenuLoader — goes through MaterialLookup.parse, which is deliberately XMaterial-backed precisely because material enum names drift across Minecraft versions (MaterialLookup's javadoc at line 17 states this rationale). A type item requirement naming a material whose constant was renamed across versions therefore fails to resolve on a server where the identical name inside a slot's item: field resolves fine, so a gate copy-pasted from a working slot definition can be permanently unsatisfiable while looking correct.

title: NbtApplier silently narrows an int_array value that NbtSchemaValidator already reported as an ERROR
fix: Gate the nbtApplier construction on the report having no errors for the nbt block, so a value the validator rejected is never written
observation: NbtSchemaValidator reports config.item.nbt.list.range and returns when an int_array entry exceeds int range (NbtSchemaValidator.java:58-64). ItemDefinitionLoader nonetheless builds the applier from the same mapping unconditionally: `NbtSchemaValidator.validate(nbtMapping, reader.report()); if (isNbtApiAvailable()) { nbtApplier = NbtApplier.applierFor(nbtMapping, reader.report()); }` (ItemDefinitionLoader.java:508-510). NbtApplier's int_array branch re-reads the value as a Long and narrows without any range recheck — `out[i] = v.intValue();` — and byte_array does the same with byteValue(). The rendered item therefore carries a silently wrapped garbage integer on every render even though /menu reload already told the admin the value was invalid; the class javadoc says it "trusts that validation and just writes", but nothing gates on whether validation actually passed.

title: MenuEditor.open calls previous.exit() instead of requestExit(), discarding an unsaved editor session
fix: Route the replacement of an existing controller through previous.requestExit() so a dirty session opens ExitPromptScreen instead of being torn down silently
observation: When a player who already has an editor open runs /menu edit again, open() replaces the controller with `EditorController previous = active.remove(player.getUniqueId()); if (previous != null) { previous.exit(); }`. EditorController.exit() (EditorController.java:129-137) unregisters the listener and closes the inventory unconditionally, while requestExit() (EditorController.java:120-126) does `if (session.dirty()) { open(new ExitPromptScreen()); } else { exit(); }`. Every other exit route — Escape, the Hub exit button, back() at the root — goes through the dirty-checked path, so this one call site is the sole way to lose unsaved material, lore, action, requirement and property edits with no warning or prompt.

title: SlotOpScreen.apply deletes an occupied destination slot when the grabbed source was cleared meanwhile
fix: Treat a null resolved source as a cancelled no-op for MOVE and COPY, and clear GridScreen's grabbed marker whenever the grabbed cell's own content is edited or cleared
observation: GridScreen.cellFor assigns the cell's edit handlers before the grab marker is applied, and the grab branch only rewrites presentation: `if (isGrab) { cell.name("&e[grabbed] slot " + index).lore(...); }` (GridScreen.java:114-117). The still-grabbed cell therefore keeps its onLeftClick into SlotEditing, so an admin can clear or delete that slot and return to the same GridScreen with `grabbed` unchanged. Shift-clicking an occupied destination then runs apply(), which re-reads `Object from = slots.get(src);` as null and for MOVE does `slots.remove(src); put(slots, dst, from);` — and put() maps a null value to `slots.remove(key)` (SlotOpScreen.java:89-95). The destination's configured item definition is deleted from the working copy even though the screen's own "Overwrites slot N" warning implied a real item was inbound.

title: GridScreen.duplicate and SlotOpScreen bypass targetFor's crafting result/grid schema and silently no-op
fix: Route duplicate() and apply() through the same crafting-aware lookup targetFor() already uses, or message the admin when a cell is not backed by the indexed slots map
observation: GridScreen.targetFor() already handles a crafting menu storing its content under named result: and grid: keys rather than indexed slots.<n>, routing those through MapKeyTarget. duplicate(int index) was never updated to match: it reads `Object source = controller.session().rawSlot(index)` and writes through `controller.session().slots()`, both of which only consult slots.<n>. On a crafting menu using the named schema, right-clicking a visibly populated result or grid cell resolves source as null and returns immediately via `if (source == null) { return; }` with no message, so duplicate silently does nothing. SlotOpScreen.apply()'s exclusive use of controller.session().slots() gives grab, move, copy and swap the same blind spot on those cells.

title: ChestMenu.close skips returnHeldItems on CloseReason.USER, destroying DepositSlotComponent items on Escape
fix: Return (or drop at the player's feet) held ItemHoldingComponent items on USER closes too — Bukkit only restores the cursor stack, never a custom inventory's slot contents
tests: DepositSlotComponentTest and DepositSlotMultiSlotStressTest both assert today's wrong behaviour and must be flipped with the fix
observation: close(Player,CloseReason) drains held items only for non-user reasons: `if (reason != CloseReason.USER) { returnHeldItems(player, reason, true); }`. A DepositSlotComponent's stack physically occupies a slot in the plugin-created Bukkit Inventory, not the player's cursor, so the javadoc's rationale ("Bukkit's normal close flow surfaces the cursor stack to the player") does not apply to it — Bukkit discards a custom inventory's slot contents on close. Verified that no other path compensates: ChestMenuCloseListener.java:70 only calls `target.onClose(event, player)`, and ChestMenu.onClose (ChestMenu.java:422-429) merely runs the user's on_close handler, never returnHeldItems. A player who deposits an item and presses Escape loses it permanently.

title: MenuFlow.switchInternal and end() abandon DepositSlotComponent items on every panel switch
fix: Close the outgoing panel's menu with a non-USER CloseReason before building the next panel, and pass an explicit reason in end(), so ItemHoldingComponent contents drain to the player
observation: switchInternal builds a fresh ChestMenu for the target panel and swaps it in without ever closing the outgoing one: `ChestMenu newMenu = builder.build(); currentMenu = newMenu; currentPanelId = panelId; newMenu.open(viewer);`. Any item sitting in a DepositSlotComponent slot on the old panel is abandoned inside the discarded Inventory. end() is no better — MenuFlow.java:153 calls `currentMenu.close(viewer)`, the reason-less overload, which routes to the USER path that finding 1 shows never returns held items. So a payment, bid, or appraisal slot inside a flow panel loses its contents on every switchTo, back, and end, and no MenuFlow code path transfers them.

title: ChestMenuCloseListener fires the outgoing menu's on_close handler during internal navigation
fix: Move the `target.onClose(event, player)` dispatch inside the same `currentMenuOf(player) == target` guard already used for the veto and untrack branches
observation: ChestMenu.open() tracks the incoming menu before calling player.openInventory(), so when a navigation triggers Bukkit's implicit close of the outgoing inventory, `MenuTracking.tracker().currentMenuOf(player) == target` is already false for that outgoing menu. The listener correctly skips the veto and untrack block in that case, but `target.onClose(event, player);` sits after the closing brace at line 70 and runs unconditionally. Every navigation into a submenu therefore fires the parent menu's YAML on_close actions — message, sound, command — as though the player had genuinely left the menu, when they only clicked through to a child screen.

title: PaginatedListPageState.itemAt never clamps a stale page after the backing list shrinks
fix: Clamp the stored page against pageCount(player, ctx) - 1 inside itemAt or currentPage, mirroring the clamp PaginatedChestMenu.render already applies
observation: itemAt uses whatever page was last stored with no upper bound against the freshly fetched list: `int idx = page * slotsPerPage + regionIndex; return idx < items.size() ? items.get(idx) : null;`. nextPage clamps on the way up, but nothing re-clamps when the list later shrinks — so after invalidate(player) runs from a cycle_sort, cycle_filter or set_search action while the viewer sits on a high page, every region cell renders null and the player sees a blank page instead of snapping back to the last valid one. PaginatedChestMenu's whole-menu pagination avoids exactly this with an explicit clamp on every render, so the two pagination systems diverge on the same trigger.

title: PaginatedControlState's four per-viewer maps never evict a departed player
fix: Clear a UUID's sortIndex, filterIndex, searchQuery and descending entries on menu close or PlayerQuitEvent instead of only on the whole-state clear driven by /menu reload
observation: The viewer state is four plain HashMaps — `private final Map<UUID, Integer> sortIndex = new HashMap<>();` plus filterIndex, searchQuery and descending — written by cycleSort, cycleFilter, setSearchQuery and toggleDirection and never removed per player. The only bulk removal is PaginatedControlRegistry.unregister/clear, which fires on /menu reload and drops the whole menu's state. Since the registry holds one state object per registered menu name for the life of the process, a public server accumulates four stale entries for every unique visitor who ever touched sort, filter or search on that menu. Growth is tied to player turnover rather than concurrent player count, so it never plateaus between reloads.

title: ChestMenu.rerenderSlot omits the wasTouched blanking that renderAll performs
fix: Have rerenderSlot check view.wasTouched() after renderOne and blank the slot and its handlers when the component rendered nothing, matching renderAll
observation: renderAll treats an untouched ChestSlotView as a deliberate no-render and clears the slot: `if (!view.wasTouched()) { inventory.setItem(entry.getKey(), null); clearHandlers(entry.getKey()); }`. rerenderSlot has no equivalent — it calls `renderOne(slot, component, viewer);` then applyFillIfEmpty and returns, never inspecting wasTouched(). PaginatedNavComponent.renderInto returns early without touching the SlotView at a page boundary by design, so refreshing such a slot through the public rerenderSlot API leaves the previous render's arrow item and its click handler in place, while the framework's own rerender() path would have cleared them. Consumers of the published builder API hit the inconsistent behaviour; internal callers use rerender() and do not.

title: ChestMenu.adoptComponentsFrom clears a slot and its handlers for a component the fresh render dropped without returning that component's held items first, destroying deposits on every rerender that drops a slot
fix: Before inventory.setItem(oldSlot, null), if the outgoing component holds items for the viewer, run the return path for that slot
tests: ChestMenuTest (fix round 1: verifies returnHeldItemsForSlot runs before the slot is cleared, no double-return path)
observation: adoptComponentsFrom (:466-478) clears a slot and its handlers for any component the fresh render dropped; if that component is an ItemHoldingComponent holding a stack, it leaves components with no return path, so returnHeldItems (:673, the close-time drain) can never reach it - the item is gone from the inventory and unreturnable the moment MenuFlow.rerender() drops a slot. Found in the Oriel 0.8.0 G1+G2 review (Critical 1) alongside the deposit-persistence work (menu-chest #1/#2, this docket's rows 1-2); FIXED in the same fix round - adoptComponentsFrom now returns via the new private returnHeldItemsForSlot (:713-740) before clearing, with no double-return path against the normal close drain.

title: Deposit-slot items are not recovered after an ungraceful shutdown (kill -9) or crash - there is no on-disk/startup-recovery path for held items, only the in-session return paths
fix: Accepted as out of scope for the 2026-09-14 decoupling wave (ruling W21): Gangland's WS2 workstream no longer parks items in Oriel menus (re-targeted onto Keystone's own keystone-inventory, R10), so no Gangland gate depends on this; tracked as an Oriel backlog item for its own roadmap
location: docs/USE-CASE-ENABLERS.md:77-86 (A3 requirement); menu-inventories/chest/src/main/java/org/luckyraven/oriel/chest/flow/MenuFlow.java, ChestMenu.java (in-session return paths only)
observation: The Oriel 0.8.0 G1+G2 review found deposit persistence had three halves: menu-chest #1 (Escape close, this docket's row 1) and #2 (panel switch, row 2) are covered by the in-session return paths and both fixed; the third half - USE-CASE-ENABLERS.md's A3, surviving a kill -9 or crash via an on-disk write plus startup recovery of any still-held deposit - was never built and has no in-session mechanism that could cover it. Orchestrator ruling W21 (2026-09-17) accepted this gap in writing rather than scheduling it inside the decoupling wave; this row exists so the acceptance is recorded, not only in a chat/ruling log.

title: Oriel's own ChestMenuCloseListener/ChestMenu pair loses held items on the same veto+disconnect and programmatic-close/menu-switch paths Keystone's keystone-inventory E6.1 found and fixed in its base MenuListener/ChestMenu
fix: Port Keystone's E6.1 round-2/3 fix shape to Oriel's own listener pair: on the vetoed tracked-close branch record a pending reopen per service/consumer, consume it on PlayerQuitEvent and return the held items with a disconnect-equivalent reason (quit fires before player data is saved); drain any pending reopen from closeAll/shutdown/reload too, not only from onQuit; give programmatic close(Player) / menu-switch a documented, tested contract for whether it returns held items (Oriel's MenuFlow already routes switches through a real CloseReason - verify it does not skip the veto/disconnect race the same way)
observation: Keystone's keystone-inventory E6.1 review (2026-09-17, Critical F1 + a fix-round-1 re-review finding) found that a menu veto followed by the player disconnecting before the scheduled reopen fires loses any held ItemHoldingComponent contents - CraftBukkit closes the inventory before PlayerQuitEvent (SPIGOT-5799), so onQuit finds nothing tracked and the item is gone; Keystone fixed this in keystone-inventory (InventoryService per-service pendingReopen, consumed atomically on quit and drained on closeAll/shutdown, E6.1 fix rounds 2-3, commit 53de9e6) but the same veto+disconnect shape exists in Oriel's own, structurally similar ChestMenuCloseListener/ChestMenu pair and was never independently checked or fixed there - this is the Oriel-track twin row the Keystone review's orchestrator ruling (W26) named for the docket step. Not exercised by any Oriel test; needs its own red-first case mirroring Keystone's InventoryServiceLifecycleTest/MenuListenerTest coverage.

title: MenuFlow.suspend()/resume() keep the old inventory handle; after an anvil/chat detour the next switchTo(same panel)/rerender() adopts into the inventory the detour already Bukkit-closed, leaving the player with no open window
fix: Track that a detour happened (a `detoured`-style flag set in suspend(), cleared only once a genuine reopen happens) and force the full close+reopen path instead of the in-place adopt/rerender path while it is set - port Keystone keystone-inventory 1.11.0's MenuFlow fix shape (commit 6ea96e5) to Oriel's own flow/MenuFlow.java
observation: Found by the Keystone keystone-inventory E6.2 review (2026-09-20, Critical 1) while porting Oriel's own flow package: suspend()/resume() only toggle a `suspended` boolean, never null or otherwise flag the live `currentMenu` handle. An external detour (anvil, sign, etc.) Bukkit-closes that inventory out from under the flow; when the caller then calls switchTo(<same panel>) (the documented re-render-in-place pattern, mirrored in Gangland's own `ShopAdminView.java:426-429`-style usage before WS1's scoreboard-only edits), MenuFlow's in-place branch (or rerender()) calls adoptComponentsFrom on an inventory that no longer has an open viewer - the player is left with no window while the flow object still thinks it is live. Keystone independently found and fixed the same bug in its own keystone-inventory base (commit 6ea96e5, a `detoured` flag): Oriel's shipped code has the identical shape at MenuFlow.java:184-192 and was never independently checked or fixed on this track. Cross-reference: this docket's row 9 (OR-CH-09, the veto+disconnect twin) - both are Oriel-track ports of Keystone keystone-inventory fixes not yet applied here. Not exercised by any Oriel test.

title: TraderMenu.open rebuilds MerchantRecipes each open, resetting maxUses so limited-stock trades are unlimited
fix: Persist per-player-per-offer use counts (or reuse the built MerchantRecipe instances) across opens instead of calling offer.toRecipe() fresh in every open()
tests: TraderMenuStressTest exercises repeated open/close but never asserts uses or maxUses, so the behaviour is unpinned
observation: open() constructs a brand-new Merchant and a brand-new recipe list on every invocation: `for (TradeOffer offer : offers) { MerchantRecipe recipe = offer.toRecipe(); recipes.add(recipe); recipeIndex.put(recipe, offer); }`. TradeOffer.toRecipe (TradeOffer.java:43-50) does `MerchantRecipe recipe = new MerchantRecipe(result.clone(), maxUses);` and never restores a prior use count, so each new instance starts at uses = 0. Minecraft enforces maxUses only within the lifetime of one MerchantRecipe instance, so an admin-configured "limited stock" or "buy once" trade is bought again simply by closing and reopening the trader — no exploit tooling required, just walking away and coming back. Every purchase beyond the intended cap is item and currency creation.

title: TraderMenu.open registers in TraderRegistry before openMerchant, whose implicit close deletes the new entry
fix: Call player.openMerchant(...) first and register afterwards, or make the close handler unregister only when the stored menu is identity-equal to the one being closed
tests: TraderMenuStressTest asserts the registry is overwritten on reopen but never registers TraderClickListener as a live listener, so it cannot observe the close-driven deletion
observation: open() runs `TraderRegistry registry = TraderSupport.registry(); registry.register(player, this); player.openMerchant(fresh, true); MenuTracking.tracker().track(player, this);` — the registry write precedes openMerchant. Bukkit's openMerchant implicitly closes whatever the player currently has open and fires InventoryCloseEvent synchronously inside that call, and TraderClickListener.onClose (TraderClickListener.java:103-111) unconditionally does `registry.unregister(player);` for any MERCHANT-type close. Opening a trader menu while one is already open therefore writes the new entry, then immediately deletes it when the old screen's close event fires. The next purchase finds no registry entry, so onTrade and onPurchase never fire while the vanilla item exchange still completes — the player trades but the menu's handlers silently do not run.

title: WorkbenchMenu, DispenserMenu, HopperMenu and TraderMenu track the menu after opening, contradicting FurnaceMenu's documented order
fix: Move MenuTracking.tracker().track(player, this) before the first render and the open call in all four types, matching FurnaceMenu
observation: WorkbenchMenu.open() runs `ensureTitleFor(player); renderAll(player); player.openInventory(inventory); MenuTracking.tracker().track(player, this);`, tracking only after the inventory is already shown; DispenserMenu.java:166-170, HopperMenu.java:170-174 and TraderMenu.java:83-86 do the same. FurnaceMenu.open (FurnaceMenu.java:219-222) deliberately does the opposite with an explicit comment: "Track before the first render so PlaceholderProviders that look up the player's current menu resolve against this furnace on open, not just after a click — mirrors ChestMenu.open." A PlaceholderProvider or on_open handler calling currentMenuOf(player) during the first render of those four types resolves the player's previous menu or null instead of the one opening, and self-corrects only on a later rerender. Note the majority of types use the later ordering, so the intended convention should be settled before the fix.

title: FurnaceProgress.max has no upper bound and overflows the short-typed furnace window property
fix: Clamp or reject max above Short.MAX_VALUE in FurnaceProgress's compact constructor, matching what the window-property protocol carries
tests: FurnaceProgressTest covers ascending/descending math and invalid args but never a large max
observation: The compact constructor validates only the lower bound: `if (max < 0) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("max must be >= 0, was " + max); }` plus a ticksPerCycle check. FurnaceMenuBuilder.fuelProgress and cookProgress (FurnaceMenuBuilder.java:171-180) pass the value through unvalidated, and FurnaceMenu.advanceProgress / pushProgressDenominators (FurnaceMenu.java:374-389, 416-420) forward it into PacketAdapter.setProperty, which becomes Minecraft's ContainerSetData field — a short. A configured max above 32767 wraps to a negative value, so the client shows a garbled or inverted burn/cook bar with no warning logged anywhere.

title: AnvilMenu dereferences AnvilGUI with no presence check, so consumers of the published oriel-anvil artifact get a bare NoClassDefFoundError
fix: Guard the AnvilBuilderFactory.create() call with a class-presence check and throw an IllegalStateException naming AnvilGUI as a required runtime dependency
observation: AnvilMenu.Builder.open() routes through getBuilder(...), which does `return AnvilBuilderFactory.create().plugin(AnvilSupport.plugin())...`, and AnvilBuilderFactory.create() (AnvilBuilderFactory.java:20-22) returns `factory.get()` where the default factory is `AnvilGUI.Builder::new` — a hard reference to net.wesjd.anvilgui.AnvilGUI with no presence check in the module. This repo's CLAUDE.md states AnvilGUI is deliberately compileOnly in menu-inventories:anvil so the published oriel-anvil Central artifact never bundles it, with menu-plugin holding the shaded copy. Any third-party consumer who depends on oriel-anvil from Central without shading AnvilGUI themselves gets a raw JVM class-loading error on the first open(player), with no Oriel-authored message identifying the missing dependency.

title: TraderMenu.returnInputItems under-counts returned because dropped accumulates across both input slots
fix: Track a per-stack dropped count inside the loop and use that in the returned calculation, adding it to the running total afterwards
observation: Inside the loop over the merchant's two input slots, leftovers are dropped and tallied into a method-scoped counter, then the return count is computed against that cumulative total: `dropped += leftover.getAmount(); } returned += stack.getAmount() - dropped;`. On the second slot's iteration, dropped already includes whatever the first slot dropped, so returned is under-counted and can go negative. Only the closing `log.debug("Returned {} item(s) to {} from trader inputs...")` diagnostic is affected — the addItem and dropItemNaturally calls move the right items — but an admin reading logs after a plugin-disable item return sees wrong numbers. No test in trader/src/test covers returnInputItems.

title: HistoryService.quote hardcodes double quotes, so the player_uuid migration no-ops on MySQL and the column is then dropped
fix: Quote identifiers through the backend's own quoteIdentifier (backticks on MySQL) instead of hardcoding double quotes, and do not treat a probe SQLException as "nothing to migrate"
tests: HistoryServiceLegacyMigrationTest covers SQLite only; no MySQL path is tested
observation: migrateLegacyColumn probes with `backend.query("SELECT player_uuid FROM " + quote(tableName) + " LIMIT 1", ...)`, and quote() is `return '"' + identifier.replace("\"", "\"\"") + '"';` with a javadoc that admits the assumption: "Double quotes for SQL-standard portability — both SQLite and MySQL (in ANSI_QUOTES mode) accept them". MySQL's default sql_mode does not include ANSI_QUOTES, so the double-quoted table name parses as a string literal and the probe throws a syntax-error SQLException even when a real legacy table exists; the catch block then does `migrated.add(menuName); return true;` and no rename happens. Keystone's AbstractJdbcBackend.applySchema afterwards runs `"ALTER TABLE " + quoteIdentifier(schema.tableName()) + " DROP COLUMN " + quoteIdentifier(drop)` (AbstractJdbcBackend.java:132-136) for every live column absent from the declared schema — correctly backtick-quoted, so it succeeds — dropping the still-present player_uuid column. Any MySQL-backed install upgrading from Oriel 0.6.x or earlier permanently loses its audit history, which is exactly the outcome this method's own javadoc says it exists to prevent.

title: HistoryService.logEvent reports audit-write failures nowhere admins are told to look
fix: Wrap the delegate call and report a failed insert through Diagnostics, mirroring what migrateLegacyColumn already does in the same class
tests: HistoryServiceSqliteTest and DatabaseFaultSinkSqliteTest exist but neither covers a failing INSERT
observation: logEvent has no try/catch and no return value — `delegate.logEvent(menuName, playerUuid, actionType, payload);` passes straight to Keystone's AuditLogService.logEvent, whose own catch only calls log.warn and never reports to Diagnostics (root cause in Keystone AuditLogService.logEvent). migrateLegacyColumn, one method down in the same file, does the opposite on failure: `Diagnostics hub = Diagnostics.active(); if (hub != null) { hub.report(rename, "history.migrate"); }`, surfacing faults through the DatabaseFaultSink-backed faults table this very module ships. A dropped deposit or return audit row — transient MySQL pool exhaustion, a closed connection — is therefore invisible in the place admins are directed to check, and DepositActions.maybeLog has no way to learn the write failed either.

title: DepositActions.encode returns an empty string on serialization failure, persisting a row indistinguishable from a zero-item snapshot
fix: Return null from encode on IOException so maybeLog can treat it as the documented no-payload case, or skip the logEvent call entirely
observation: maybeLog calls `history.logEvent(menuName, ctx.player().getUniqueId(), actionType, encode(snapshot));` unconditionally, and encode swallows a serialization failure into a valid-looking value: `catch (IOException ex) { log.warn(...); return ""; }`. HistoryRow's javadoc defines payload as either the Base64 blob or null meaning "no item payload", so an empty string is not the documented failure representation. The audit table then holds a row that reads as a legitimate zero-item deposit when it actually records a failed serialization, quietly corrupting that row's meaning for anyone auditing item custody later, even though a console warning was logged at the time.

title: A failed database reconnect on /menu reload aborts reloadLifecycleBeans and leaves AnimationTicker cancelled
fix: Catch and log the connection failure inside ManagedDatabaseBackend.open() rather than rethrowing, so the reload cascade continues to the LIFECYCLE phase
observation: ManagedDatabaseBackend.open() rethrows a connection failure as `throw new IllegalStateException("Database backend '" + type + "' could not connect", ex);` at line 125. Keystone's BeanFactory.reloadLifecycleBeans (BeanFactory.java:333-350) runs three bare loops — onPreClear, onClear, then `for (BeanLifecycle bean : forward) { bean.onInitialize(false); }` — with no per-bean try/catch, so that exception aborts the forward loop. AnimationConfig is `@Configuration(phase = Phase.LIFECYCLE)`, ordered after PersistenceConfig's DATABASE phase, so its AnimationTicker has already had its BukkitTask cancelled by the earlier onClear pass and never receives the onInitialize call that would restart it. An ordinary admin mistake such as a mistyped mysql host therefore silently freezes every animated menu for every viewer until a later reload succeeds end to end, with only ReloadCommand's generic failure message shown.

title: UpdateChecker is constructed with a hardcoded resourceId of 0, making /menu download and the startup check permanently inert
fix: Add a resource-id key to config.yml and pass it through KernelConfig.updateChecker, or remove DownloadCommand and UpdateCheckBootstrap until Oriel is published
observation: The bean method returns `new UpdateChecker(plugin, permissionManager, pluginName, 0);` with the resource id as a literal zero and no config key anywhere to override it. Keystone's UpdateChecker documents that value as a sentinel — "resourceId is treated as a sentinel: anything <= 0 short-circuits every method to a safe no-op" (UpdateChecker.java:31) — and gates on `return resourceId > 0;` (UpdateChecker.java:183). So /menu download always reports that Oriel is already up to date and UpdateCheckBootstrap never queries SpigotMC, on every server running this jar. A fully wired, help-documented command and a boot-time check are shipped dead with nothing telling the admin they are inert.

title: ImportService is wired to context::reloadBeans, so /menu import closes every online player's open menu
fix: Wire ImportService's reload callback to context::reloadMenus, the narrower path EditorConfig's MenuReloader already uses for the same scenario
observation: The bean is built as `return new ImportService(importers, menusDir, templatesDir, context::reloadBeans);`. OrielContext.reloadBeans() runs the full BeanLifecycle cascade, which bounces the database pool, restarts the animation ticker, and force-closes every online player's open menu with CloseReason.RELOAD via DefaultOpenMenuTracker.onPreClear — all merely to make newly imported YAML visible. EditorConfig's MenuReloader deliberately calls the narrower context.reloadMenus() for the same "a menu file just changed" case. An admin running /menu import therefore interrupts every unrelated player's menu session and briefly drops the database connection.

title: DevPaginatedMenuConfig's javadoc claims a Phase.DATABASE pin its bare @Configuration annotation does not apply
fix: Add phase = Phase.DATABASE to the annotation to match the documented invariant, or delete the demo config as its own comment already proposes
observation: The class javadoc states the class is "pinned to Phase.DATABASE (between KERNEL and CONFIG) so the source is in the registry before MenuConfigService (CONFIG phase) fires its onInitialize pass", and warns that without it "a CONFIG-phase intra-phase ordering race could cause the YAML loader to log a spurious config.paginated.source warning". The actual annotation at line 30 is a bare `@Configuration`, which defaults to Phase.CONFIG — the same phase as ConfigLoaderConfig's MenuConfigService — while the sibling DemoComponentsConfig and DemoItemProvidersConfig do carry the explicit `@Configuration(phase = Phase.DATABASE)` the comment describes. Since devPaginated(MenuRegistry) has no bean-parameter dependency edge on menuConfigService, their relative order within CONFIG falls to incidental scan order. Impact is limited to a spurious warning for a dev-only demo menu already marked for pre-release removal.

title: give_permission and take_permission bypass the allow_elevated_actions gate that locks down op and permission
fix: Gate both PermissionActions registrations behind ActionParser's elevatedActionsGate, warning and no-opping when allow_elevated_actions is false
observation: PermissionActions registers both actions into the ActionRegistry with only a blank-node check before returning `ctx -> permissions.add(ctx.player(), node);` and `ctx -> permissions.remove(ctx.player(), node);`. The functionally equivalent built-in op and permission actions are hard-gated by allow_elevated_actions, which defaults to false and whose config.yml comment says to leave it off "unless you trust every menu author on the server"; ActionParser refuses them with a warning until an admin opts in. PermissionActions consults no such gate, and its own javadoc notes the core permission action is the scoped alternative "it revokes the node again after the command runs" — so the ungated action is the strictly more powerful one, granting nodes permanently. Any menu author, including one using the in-game editor, can write give_permission with an arbitrary node while the guarded path stays locked. Exploiting it requires menu-authoring access, but the whole purpose of the gate is to bound exactly that actor.

title: EconomyActions discards the Vault transaction result, so a failed take_money still lets the rest of the chain reward the player
fix: Check the boolean returned by economy.withdraw/deposit and cancel the click or abort the chain when it is false, instead of discarding it
observation: Both registrations return statement-expression lambdas against ClickHandler's void onClick — `return ctx -> economy.deposit(ctx.player(), amount);` and `return ctx -> economy.withdraw(ctx.player(), amount);` — so the transactionSuccess-derived boolean from Keystone's EconomyProvider is thrown away. ActionParser.chain runs handlers with `for (ClickHandler h : handlers) h.onClick(ctx);` and never aborts on failure, so a menu whose on_left_click is take_money followed by a reward action hands out the reward even when the player could not be charged — nothing requires an author to pair take_money with a money requirement, and the demo presents that pairing only as the recommended pattern. The same gap applies to the documented check-then-charge flow: EconomyRequirements only ever calls the read-only has(), and RequirementHook has already committed to running the gated handler by the time on_success fires, so a withdraw that fails for a backend reason still yields a free reward. ClickHandler's javadoc documents ctx.cancel() for exactly this signal and EconomyActions never calls it.

title: give_money and take_money accept non-finite amounts because min(0) cannot reject NaN or Infinity
fix: Add a Double.isFinite check alongside the existing amount<=0 guard and report a config error for a non-finite value
observation: Both actions parse with `NodeReader.of(mapping, report).get("give_money").asDouble().min(0).required().orElse(0)`. Keystone's DoubleAccess.min rejects only via a `value < min` comparison, and by IEEE 754 every comparison against NaN is false while `Infinity < 0` is also false, so both sail through; the follow-up guard `if (amount <= 0) { return NO_OP; }` fails to catch them for the same reason. A YAML amount that overflows a double, such as 1e999, resolves to positive infinity and reaches economy.deposit unchecked, and a NaN amount reaches the Vault call with undefined balance behaviour. This is a robustness gap rather than a privilege escalation — a menu author who can write the amount could already write a very large finite number — but a non-finite value can corrupt an economy plugin's stored balance irrecoverably rather than merely inflating it. Root cause of the permissive parse is in Keystone's NodeReader.
